abstract: In order to improve system performance and reduce receiver hardware complexity and cost, we investigate a new multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) scheme combining maximal-ratio transmit and receiver antenna selection combining (the MRT/RAS scheme). In this scheme, a single receive antenna, which maximizes the received signal-to-noise (SNR) at the receiver, is selected for demodulation. The closed-form outage probability and the bit error rate (BER) of the MRT/RAS system are presented. The simulation demonstrates that the MRT/RAS scheme can achieve a full diversity order, as if all the receive antennas were used. It is shown that the TAS/MRC scheme outperforms some more complex space-time codes of the same spectral efficiency. The analytical results are verified by simulation

articleTitle: A Study on Wireless Sensor Networks Location
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: On the study of location system, a novel location estimation scheme for wireless sensor network was proposed. The location estimation scheme has two steps. In the first step unknown nodes estimate the initial positions for sensor nodes by obtaining location information from anchors, and in the second step unknown nodes refines estimated positions by exchange location information with their neighbors to implement refinement location. Moreover, in our simulation reasonable and accurate locations can be obtained and the average position error sharply decreased

articleTitle: Generation of Chaotic Frequency Hopping Codes and Its Application in Communications
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Based on the logistic map and the idea of symbolic dynamics, chaotic frequency hopping (FH) codes are generated by using the return map. The codes have good performance, and are more immune to prediction and interception. Furthermore, an FH-CSK communication system is designed and realized. The theoretical analysis and simulation results show that the system has good performance over the AWGN and multipath channels

articleTitle: Capacity Estimation for an MF-CDMA Cellular Model Based on LEO Satellite Constellation
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Through analyzing the capacity of an MF-CDMA cellular communication network based on LEO satellite constellation, this paper gives some suggestions to develop mobile communications based on LEO satellites. According to the characteristics of MF-CDMA, possible co-channel interference is taken into account based on a comprehensive interference analysis model including the analysis of internal and external interference, which could be the main factor to limit the user capacity. This is because that the frequency resource appears to be quite limited while the satellite power is usually able to satisfy the requirement, moreover, controlling the downlink inter-channel interference is not so difficult. By assuming some crucial parameters combined with the practice of the Globalstar system, the number of the active channels and traffic capacity are estimated. The results indicate that the advantages of MF-CDMA are obvious and it can satisfy the expected traffic requirement

articleTitle: S_Firewall: A Firewall in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) have wide applications both in military and civil fields. However, when deployed in untended/hostile area, WSNs may suffer all kinds of attacks like flooding, sinkhole, etc. To apply WSNs more practically and wildly, some secure countermeasures must be deployed in WSNs. In this paper, we design a kind of firewall scheme, which is based on mobile agent, to isolate the intruder with less communication overhead and memory cost. The S_Firewall can be generated automatically, distributively and in real time when network-wide attacks happen. The paper also proposes a route restoring scheme by local repair and makes a performance analysis by prototype implementation of S_Firewall

articleTitle: Searching Algorithm of the Optimal Sensor Set in Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper considers the problem of finding the optimal sensor set in an unknown environment with many redundant sensors. In this paper, an optimal searching algorithm based on genetic algorithm is proposed during the initial planning phase in sensor network. This algorithm can extend the network lifetime by maintaining the same coverage rate of the network with a necessary set of working sensors and turn off redundant ones. The simulation output shows that the algorithm can achieve optimal node selection in the target area and improve the sensor ability of the whole network at a low cost relatively

articleTitle: An On-Demand Clustering Mechanism for Hierarchical Routing Protocol in Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Clustering is widely used in ad hoc networks. The most important function of clustering is to provide management of large networks and assign the channel effectively. To maintain the hierarchical topology, the existing clustering mechanisms bring a lot of communication due to movement of the mobility and disappearance of nodes in the network, so there is vast control overhead. To avoid the problem, an on-demand clustering routing protocol (OCRP) is proposed. It eliminates the phase for clustering, and merges this phase with data transmission phase. OCRP adds a field for every data packet to identify five clustering states. Each node analyzes the clustering state field in the received packets, and decides how to switch its own clustering state

articleTitle: A New Method for Detection of LDPC Coded GMSK Modulated Signals
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper a new method for detection of LDPC coded, GMSK modulated signals will be proposed. Detection technique is based on Laurent decomposition of CPM signal into PAM pulses. At the receiver, the signal is passed through a filter matched to a PAM pulse with highest energy. Thereafter to eliminate effect of other pulses, a linear equalizer and a turbo like equalizer combined with LDPC decoder will be used. The performance of designed receiver is shown that is very close to optimum maximum likelihood receiver but its complexity is much smaller

articleTitle: Indoor Localization Scheme in Wireless Sensor Networks Using Spatial Information
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Position information of individual nodes is crucial for many advanced functions including routing, querying and computer security forensics in wireless sensor networks. Most of the existing localization algorithms in wireless sensor networks are designed for outdoor environment and few of them can get a reasonable localization precision in indoor environment. This paper presents a novel indoor localization scheme which uses the spatial connective information to filter distorted messages, so as to improve the positioning precision. We establish an indoor positioning dome system, make performance comparison with other schemes and fully prove the advantages of our proposed indoor scheme

articleTitle: Cooperative Transmission in the Wireless Sensors Network: Realization and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: We consider energy is a limited resource in wireless sensor networks (WSN) so that energy consumption must be minimized while satisfying given throughput requirements. In this context, we proposed a method to realize the cooperative transmission scheme in the single-hop WSN and analyzed the energy efficiency and throughput of this method. The energy consumption has taken into account both the transmission energy and the circuit processing energy, and throughout the analysis we emphasized on the capability condition of the cooperative transmission. And the analysis results showed that the cooperative transmission can increase the energy-efficiency when the sink is far away from the CNs, and also this scheme can keep the throughput of the system in a stable level with different values of SNR

articleTitle: A New Channel Tracking Algorithm Based on Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The estimation of a time-varying multipath fading channel is a difficult task for the receiver. Its performance can be improved if an appropriate channel estimation filter is used according to the prior knowledge of the fading channel. We propose an algorithm which uses the Kalman filter based on Clarke's model to track the time-varying multipath fading channel. To reduce the complexity of the high-dimensional Kalman filter for channel estimation of the paths, we use a low-dimensional Kalman filter for the estimation of each path. We investigate how to estimate the channel by the Kalman filter in the pilot-aided wireless system. Simulations show this algorithm is effective for the estimation of the fading channel when the performance of the channel estimation is presented in terms of the mean-square error (MSE)

articleTitle: A Novel Timing Estimation Method Based on Symmetrical & Conjugate Prefix in OFDM System
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A novel timing estimation method in OFDM system is proposed, which is based on symmetrical & conjugate prefix, and the expression of likelihood function is presented. Sharp correlation curve of symbol timing can be obtained using the symmetrical and conjugate character of prefix. Simulation shows that the proposed method can achieve a more accurate timing offset estimation than that based on cycle prefix

articleTitle: A Distributed Heuristics of Localization in Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: High accuracy, low computational cost and infrequent information exchange are three basic requirements for distributed localization algorithm in sensor networks. In this paper, we first propose an optimized triangulation heuristics to locate neighbor nodes in an optimal sequence such that the probability of wrong location selection can be minimized and localization accuracy can be improved to certain extent. Next, the available distributed localization algorithm is improved by introducing confidence index, a metric which helps set up the best shortest path for locating remote sensor nodes. Simulation results show that the method can give satisfactory performance without excessive computational and communication costs

articleTitle: A Method for Improving MAC Level Fairness on IEEE802.11DCF
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: IEEE 802.11, which is one of the most widely used wireless LAN standard protocol, employs binary exponential back-off (BEB) for reducing packet collisions. Although the BEB can avoid effectively packet collision by a simple mechanism, transmission unfairness arises under the high traffic environment and/or inequality of numbers of neighboring terminals situation. This paper discusses about relations between unfairness and aboves, and proposes a method of frame-burst transmission with adaptive and autonomous controlling for improving fairness in keeping compatibility with legacy IEE E802.11 DCF terminals. From the results of computer simulations, it is reported that our technique improves fairness effectively with no performance degradation

articleTitle: The Waiting Time Distribution of a Pareto Service Self-Similar Queuing Model for Wireless Network Nodes
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Research within the last decade on network measurement has been shown to exhibit self-similarity property in Ethernet, VBR video. Recent research find wireless network node has also self-similar nature. Appropriate service distribution of these sources may be heavy-tailed service distributions. A difficult with heavy-tailed service distribution queuing model is that they may not have closed-from, analytic Laplace transforms, such as Pareto distribution etc. This makes those methods using the Laplace transform challenging. This paper proposes a method for analyzing the waiting time distribution via hyperexponential distributions fitting technique combined with Laplace transform. The waiting time distribution with exponential interarrival and Pareto service distribution queuing model was derived and verified via simulations. Numerical results show the method has reliable accuracy

articleTitle: Adaptive Cross-Layer Routing for HWN with Dedicated Relay Station
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The ultimate goals for heterogeneous hybrid wireless networks are to provide different users with high-data rates, mixed traffic and QoS support. There are two types of wireless networks within the personal communication context. One is a cellular based network and the other is the emerging ad-hoc wireless network. A cellular network has reliable communication performance, with mobiles being connected through base stations while in a low-cost, plug-and-play ad-hoc network, wireless nodes communicate with one another directly without infrastructure support. In this study, we have investigated both resource management and routing strategies for hybrid wireless network with dedicated relay stations. An introduction and theoretical analysis on hybrid wireless network's capacity, access method and routing constraints are presented first. A cross layer scheme called adaptive hybrid routing with relay station and detailed hybrid traffic delivery models are then presented. Simulation results indicate that the traffic over this novel hybrid wireless network is managed more efficiently when using the proposed algorithm

articleTitle: A Distributed Weight-Based Clustering Algorithm for WSNs
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Cluster-based routing protocol has been demonstrated as a good way to meet the requirements of wireless sensor networks (WSNs), such as scalability, lifetime constraint and energy-efficiency in LEACH. On one hand, the creation of clusters can lower energy consumption within a cluster by performing data fusion to decrease the amount of sensed data forwarded to BS (base station). On the other hand, the formation of cluster can consume lots of energy and then increase additional overhead. Therefore cluster formation algorithm which decides how to select cluster and how to schedule nodes is crux in cluster-based related routing protocols. In the paper, we propose a distributed weight-based clustering algorithm for WSNs which takes battery usage, load balancing and MAC functionality into consideration. Simulation results demonstrate the energy-efficiency of the proposed algorithm

articleTitle: Design of Video NLOS Communication System Using MIMO-OFDM Based on IEEE802.16a Standard
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Rapid development in the area of broadband wireless communications demands wireless video services. The maximal challenges of transmitting video over wireless channels are non-line-of-sight (NLOS) fading deteriorate and higher data rates requirement. Fortunately, the 802.16a standard supports licensed and license-exempt spectra between 2 and 11 GHz, which is especially useful for NLOS cases. On the other hand, multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems provide higher capacity, higher data rates and lower error rate than standard single-input single-output (SISO) systems. So in order to solve the problem of video signal transmission on NLOS wireless channels, this paper presents the design of MIMO-OFDM system based on IEEE 802.16a standard. By using Alamouti's ST block code (STBC) transmission diversity at transmit antennas and (maximum ratio combing) MRC diversity at receive antennas, high data rates can be gotten. Experiment results showed that our proposed system can achieve very good performance, and the system with more antennas got a significant PSNR improvement over none diversity situation

articleTitle: Turbo Receiver for MIMO CDMA in Flat Fading Channel
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) (G.J. Foschini and M.J. Gans, 1998) CDMA system that employs space-time turbo codes is considered to enhance the system capacity. The turbo receiver introduced is able to combat the complicated interference mixture in this system. To evaluate the performance of the turbo receiver this paper focus on the performance analysis on the synchronous flat fading channel

articleTitle: Optimal Linear Precoder Design for Space-Time Block Coded Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Taking the pairwise error probability (PEP) as the performance criterion and exploiting the channel covariance information at the transmitter, this paper studies the optimal linear precoder design of the correlated multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) wireless system. The precoder can be used along with any space-time block codes (STBC), which is an extension of Y. Zhao et al. (2004) . The optimal beamforming direction of the precoder is proved to match the structure of STBC and transmit correlation matrix. The optimal power allocation scheme is related to transmit correlation matrix, receive correlation matrix and STBC. The quasi-orthogonal space-time block codes (QSTBC) is taken as an illustration to investigate the performance of the optimal precoder

articleTitle: A Novel Iterative Control Variates Algorithm for Efficient Simulation in AWGN Channels
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, we propose a fast convergent simulation algorithm for additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel which can obtain the unbiased and effective estimators of bit error rate (BER) and amplitude of the transmitted signal (TSA). It utilizes a certain cumulative distribution function as the control variate. Compared with Monte-Carlo (MC) methods, this algorithm does not require knowing TSA while its estimator of BER has a lower variance. Its estimator of TSA also has a lower variance than traditional methods. The simulation result demonstrates the conclusion, viz. both the variance of BER's estimator and that of TSA's estimator present inverse ratio to square of simulation data number

articleTitle: On-Demand Software Streaming System for Embedded System
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Many embedded computers are running with extremely limited resources and the need for optimizing resource utilization is increasing. In this paper we present the design and implementation of software streaming system that can reduce user waiting time and improve storage utilization. While traditional operating system loads program from local storage, software streaming system loads it from a remote server. The software streaming server divides executable file into basic code blocks and sends only the required code blocks instead of the whole file. We have implemented the streaming system on the embedded Linux using a streaming file system. Experimental results show that our streaming system can save storage up to 50%. Using our software streaming technique, embedded system can provide shorter waiting time to users when using new application as compared to traditional system

articleTitle: A Novel Kalman-MLSD Receiver Over Fast Fading Channel
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A novel adaptive reduced-complexity maximum likelihood sequence detection (MLSD) receiver based on per-survivor processing (PSP) algorithm and decision feedback algorithm (DF) over fast fading mobile channel with BPSK modulation is proposed in this paper. The adaptive channel tracking is implemented by a novel simplified Kalman filter bank with very short pilot tone. Computer simulations show that this receiver is a good trade-off between the performance and complexity on fast fading mobile channels

articleTitle: A Novel Demodulation Method for Chaotic Parameter Modulation
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper proposes a particle filter to demodulate the chaotic parameter modulation (CPM) signal CPM embeds the signal of transmission in the bifurcating parameter of a chaotic dynamical system, and uses the wide-band output of the chaotic system as the transmitted signal. As the bifurcating parameter of the chaotic dynamical system is unknown and the demodulation problem is just a system identification problem. Conventional methods like extended Kalman filter (EKF) and least mean square (LMS) have relatively poor performance. Incorporating Rao-Blackwellisaion (RB) and roughening noise method, particle filtering can be used to estimate the parameter sequentially. Simulation results confirm that the proposed particle filter has the improved performance compared to the EKF and LMS

articleTitle: Committees-WiCOM2006
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Provides a listing of current committee members.

articleTitle: Welcome
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Presents the welcome message from the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: Copyright - WiCOM2006
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The following topics were dealt with: wireless communications; mobile computing; ad hoc networks; mobile IP; sensor networks; UWB; multimedia; data management; MIMO; OFDM; mesh networks; coding; detection; modulation; antennas; signal processing; channel models; network layer protocols; media access protocol; congestion control; network analysis; and security

articleTitle: A Novel Location-Based Routing Algorithm for Mobile Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: To improve the performance of route overhead and packet dropped rate of routing algorithms in mobile ad hoc networks, a location-based grid routing (LBGR) algorithm is presented. By node position information, the LBGR algorithm employs a grid-constructed trajectory instead of node ID in forwarding packets. Based on the position relationship of nodes and downstream grids, each intermediate node infers the next hop to relay packets. Therefore, it can adapt to frequent and unpredictable topology changes in the presence of high mobility and greatly enhance the robustness of route maintenance. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can reduce route overhead, packet dropped rate and the average number of hops per path

articleTitle: Viterbi Algorithm Based Frequency Offset Estimation for GMSK
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A new nondata-aided frequency offset estimation method has been proposed for GMSK which is based on Viterbi algorithm to remove the information phase of the complex envelope signal. It has wide frequency offset estimation range, and its feedforward structure made itself simple digital implementation. Its complexity would be controlled by the Viterbi algorithm parameter. Simulation results have shown the validity of the algorithm in frequency offset estimation. At last, the normalized mean square errors (MSE) performance of the algorithm has also been proposed in additive white Gaussian noise channel

articleTitle: QoS Routing in IPv6 with Link-Utilization-Ratio Single Metric
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Quality-of-service routing (QoSR) is a challenging NP-hard problem of IPv6 networks. For the sake of satisfying QoS requests of future multimedia applications, a novel LMA (link-utilization-ratio metric based routing Algorithm) is proposed. It takes only a single metric called LUR (link-utilization-ratio) as the link cost, which is advertised suitably by OSPFv3 LSAs of IPv6. It computes routing by extending Dijkstra's method with the invariable complexity of O(|E|+|V|log|V|). It takes the characteristics of IPv6 into account. It favors paths with lower delay, fewer hops and higher link availability. It tries to bypass the congestive path and decrease routing overhead. Theoretical analysis proves that routing with LUR metric can bring performance improvements of other related routing metrics. A formula is provided as the criterion of choosing a better next hop to route packets. Extensive simulations show that, LMA not only outperforms the original OSPF scheme and its variants such as SWP and WSP in terms of average link-availability-ratio, average path delay and average path hop-count, but also has good adaptability to large-scale networks

articleTitle: A New Resource Allocation Scheme for Downlink OFDM Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of subcarrier allocation in OFDM systems. As we know, for single-user OFDM systems, some algorithms can be used to find the resource allocation that minimizes the total transmit power. In the multiuser OFDM systems, however, the subcarrier allocation is much more complex. In our paper, we suggest an algorithm which adopts a new assignment strategy. Firstly, we separate all the subcarriers into several resource blocks, then, we use some single user allocation algorithms to allocate non-conflicted blocks to multiple users. Finally, according to the principle of power minimization, we try to resolve the conflict problem coming from the situation that a block may be assigned to some users at the same time. Simulation results indicate that the performance of our algorithm is better than that of the optional allocation while the complexity is reduced

articleTitle: The Performance Analysis of Non-Primitive Turbo Codes in MIMO System Over Flat Fading Channel
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: So far almost all the research work on turbo codes focus on primitive turbo code (PTC). In multiple input multiple output (MIMO) system this paper concentrates on the research of non-primitive turbo code (NOPTC) over flat fading channel. It shows that NOPTC outperforms PTC at any size SIR. Thus NOPTC promotes both capacity and reliability of the communications in MIMO system. This paper concludes as well there is no direct proportion between the state-number and the BER performance of turbo code

articleTitle: Fourth-Order MUSIC Algorithm Based on Minimum Redundant Virtual Extended Array
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A novel forth-order multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm was proposed based on the virtual array technique. Since the effective array aperture is extended according to the higher-order steering vector expression, a virtual spatial covariance matrix is derived using the forth-order cumulants. In this way, the redundant information contained in the cumulants are removed, and the computational complexity is reduced for the dimension of the virtual covariance matrix is decreased, which is equal to the number of the virtual array elements. Numerical results show that for Gaussian signals, the performance of the second-order methods is optimal. However, for non-Gaussian signals, the direction estimation variance of the proposed method is decreased and the resolution probability of two close signals is improved, compared to those of the second-order MUSIC algorithm

articleTitle: A Improved Algorithm for Minimizing Preemption Cost in MPLS Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, we propose an improved heuristic algorithm for the well-known optimization formulation based on versatile preemption policy, which can minimize the preemption cost with high accuracy and less computational intractability. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm significantly outperforms the heuristic recently proposed in the literature

articleTitle: Two-Hop Two-Slot CDMA Uplink - Multi-Cell Considerations
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A multihop scheme to increase the uplink capacity of CDMA cellular systems is proposed in this paper. In such a system mobile nodes are divided into two groups: those who are close to base station can communicate with base station directly and those who are far away from base station use the first group as relays. Time slots are alternatively used by these two groups. We inspect the throughput of such a system by considering the multicell interference and compare it with that of single-hop CDMA system. We find significant throughput increase if the cell is splitted by a suitable splitting factor

articleTitle: Homomorphic Encryption Scheme of the Rational
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The existing homomorphic encryption scheme is based on ring of the integer, and the possible operators are restricted to addition and multiplication only. In this paper, a new operation is defined - similar modul. Base on the similar modul, the number sets of the homomorphic encryption scheme is extended to rational, and the possible operators are extended to addition, subtraction, multiplication and division. Our new approach provides a practical ways of implementation because of the extension of the operators and the number sets

articleTitle: A Novel Pre-FFT Beamforming for an OFDM System with an Antenna Array in WLAN
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, a new pre-fast Fourier transformation (FFT) beamforming approach is proposed for an orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) system with an antenna array in wireless local area network (WLAN). Compared with the OFDM system based on traditional beamforming or principle eigen-vector beamforming, it can offer almost the same performance with significant reduction in system structure as well as computational complexity. In addition, it outperforms the system with a switched-beam beamformer. Simulations are conducted to show the effectiveness of the proposed approach

articleTitle: Market-Based Adaptive Task Scheduling for Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper designs a microeconomic system for task scheduling in wireless sensor networks by virtue of the migration of mobile agents. Further, it proposes a market-based adaptive task scheduling algorithm, named MATS, which schedules tasks to the set of optimal nodes by adjusting the energy price of nodes and modifying the nodes' roles. The simulation in the scenario of target tracking demonstrates that MATS is adaptable to the changing network conditions and realizes an efficient allocation of energy resources by regulating the energy consumption of nodes. Compared with the static scheduling algorithm, MA TS impressively promotes the energy efficiency at the trivial cost of tracking accuracy

articleTitle: Joint ICI and Noise Reduction in OFDM Using a New Windowing Scheme
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper presents a new windowing scheme that effectively reduces the joint effect of intercarrier interference (ICI) resulting from frequency offset and additive noise in orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing. The transmitter does not need to be modified, subcarrier orthogonality in the receiver is preserved, and the receiver discrete Fourier transform size can be retained. The simulation results show that the new proposed window has a better performance than the common raised-cosine window, "better than" raised-cosine window and the maximally flat (MF) window

articleTitle: IMBP: An Interference Control Topology Algorithm Based on Interference Measure in Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Topology control has been well studied as a hotspot in wireless ad hoc networks. However, due to the strictly limited resources, few topology control methods take into account lowering interference of the entire network as the main goal. This paper proposes an interference-minimized control topology algorithm (IMBP) based on path-interference measure for ad hoc networks. Derived from the concept of measure, the IMBP presents a new metric that quantifies the degree of interference of the entire network, and gives an algorithm of computing node interference measure (CNIM), then obtains the interference-minimized network topology while preserving the connectivity of ad hoc networks. Our extensive simulation results show that IMBP algorithm can significantly reduce interference and improve the connectivity of ad hoc networks

articleTitle: A New Reduced-Complexity ML Joint Detection Algorithm Based Sphere Decoder for LS-CDMA System
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A new reduced-complexity joint detection algorithm based on sphere decoder for LS-CDMA system is proposed in this paper. This algorithm can approach ML performance in polynomial complexity. Special zero correlation window property of LS code can reduce complexity of this algorithm greatly. Simulation indicates it is more insensitive to the choice of initial radius. Thus, by making the choice of radius sufficiently large, the ML solution is guaranteed with low complexity, even for large constellations. We then extend this joint detection algorithm to MIMO case and compare it with MMSE, ZF multicode detectors. Numerical results show performance of this algorithm is good even at very high speed such as 160 Km/h, this give us some insights on developing high efficient practical joint detection algorithm for further LS-CDMA system

articleTitle: Multistage Parallel Interference Cancellation Based on Chase Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A key issue in a multistage parallel interference cancellation (PIC) scheme is to improve the hard decision accuracy after matched filters (MFs). For achieving this purpose, most PIC schemes focus on choosing the suitable weight for each user in each stage but keeping the hard decision values after MFs intact. This paper presents a new PIC scheme that uses Chase algorithm to edit the possible hard decision combinations and selects the one minimizing a cost function as the final hard decision result for performing the interference cancellation. Performance and complexity comparisons are presented among Chase-PIC, normalized least-mean-square adaptive multistage PIC (NLMS-PIC) schemes and their variants. A new PIC scheme using NLMS as the earlier stages and Chase in the later stages is proposed, which can achieve a better performance than multistage NLMS-PIC but with lower complexity

articleTitle: Underwater Acoustic Frequency Demodulation System Based on High-Q Filter
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Since underwater acoustic frequency-hopping (FH) communication system requires high resolution of frequency, an implementation method based on high-Q filter is proposed in this paper. Firstly, frequency demodulation system is briefly introduced. According to the given performance requirements of the filter, different implementation methods of the filter are compared. The equiripple approximation method with maximal error minimization principle is used to design FIR filter. Then the coefficients of FIR filter are obtained through MATLAB simulation. The digital signal processor TMS320C5416 made by TI Co. is used to implement the filter in the simulation

articleTitle: Study and Analysis of an Error Resilient Technique in H.264 Video Using Flexible Macroblock Grouping
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: An important demand in video streaming industry today is the ability to code error resilient digital video and the error concealment techniques adopted by the video coding standards. The H.264/AVC is an emerging video standard being developed jointly by the Video Coding Experts Group (VCEG) and the Moving Pictures Experts Group (MPEG) as the Joint Video Team (JVT). This new video coding standard defines some very powerful features that make it promising for the next generation Internet applications like video streaming. Apart from significant improvements in compression performance, this standard is also more 'network friendly' and provides more features for error resilience. This is of significant importance to business applications based on real time video streaming such as video conferencing and Internet based video-on-demand, where packet losses introduced by bottleneck network links and network congestion can cause significant video quality performance degradation. In this paper, we study the error resilience techniques provided by the emerging H.264 video standard. We study the effects of slice coding on transmitted video and also analyze the concept of slice groups and flexible macroblock ordering (FMO), which are error resilience techniques adopted in the H.264 video coding standard

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency Comparison of SACK, Tahoe, Reno and NewReno Over Ad Hoc Network Based on Analytic Hierarchy Process
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: TCP, originally designed for reliable, fixed networks, interprets all packet loss into network congestion. However, this never holds in ad hoc networks. Mobility, channel error or node exhaustibility induced errors may all lead to unnecessary energy costs in TCP. Our work is prompted by the lack of energy efficiency evaluation methods concerning the overall performance improvement, as opposed to partial enhancement in algorithm optimization. We exploit the energy consumption behaviors of SACK, Tahoe, Reno and NewReno option over ad hoc networks. Simulation results indicate that SACK out-performs other three options in the case of mobility and channel error while Tahoe, Reno and NewReno perform better than SACK when node exhaustibility happens. It is also observed that node exhaustibility affects the energy consuming behavior of the whole network most. Application of analytic hierarchy process (AHP) to those simulation results leads to the final recommendation of SACK as the most energy efficient option

articleTitle: A Call Admission Control Scheme Using Statistical Priority Queue
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In modern wireless networks, call admission control (CAC) has received a lot of attention because of its central role for quality of service (QoS) provision. In this paper, a new admission control scheme using statistical priority queue (SQCAC) is proposed. Its objective is to get an optimal overall satisfaction for the customers in terms of an objective function defined in this paper. In SQCAC, handoff calls and new calls occupy the queue in basic station (BS) statistically. Handoff calls are given a higher probability to occupy the queue than new calls when the available bandwidth is used out. SQCAC can also provide a tradeoff between call block probability (CBP) and call dropping probability (CDP)

articleTitle: Novel Rate Control Scheme Based on System Load and Channel Quality
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, we propose an adaptive uplink rate control scheme based on the reverse activity bit (RAB) setting at base station (BS) and channel quality mobile station (MS) undergoes. According to the RAB and the increment of traffic to pilot ratio (T2P) broadcasted by BS, each MS adaptively adjusts its rate based on the maximum supported T2P in a deterministic manner according to the channel quality indication (CQI). It is proved by system level simulation that the proposed adaptive scheme can enlarge system throughput while guaranteeing quality of service (QoS) and fairness

articleTitle: A Study Towards Enhanced Reliability Performance of Remote Control and Monitoring Application Over Commercial Wireless Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Remote control and monitoring systems provide many useful operating advantages in industrial automation and demand highly reliable and secure communication means. Their widespread use is, however, limited because of the high cost of current communications in use making them economically infeasible. Hence, there is a need to develop new low cost communication and control concepts by making such solutions economically feasible. In this paper, we present a scheme for implementing reliable wireless communication links for application of remote control and monitoring system based on current available commercial wireless communication networks, e.g. GPRS/EDGE/UMTS. The reliability enhancement over wireless networks has been proposed and its performance has been studied. This paper examines the proposed solution by means of both analytical and numerical evaluation, and has shown that the demanded reliability performance can be met by using only commercial wireless communication networks

articleTitle: The Multi-Stage Chaotic Secure Communication System Applied in Radio Frequency Channel
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper a multi-stage chaotic secure communication system applied in radio frequency( RF) channel is proposed. This scheme adopts multi-stage chaotic asynchronous cascades in order to improve the traditional chaotic masking method which is tended to be broken the security can be enhanced obviously. The systematic structure of the receiver can be simplified by the two parallel driving signals are transmitted to the receiver simultaneously after implementing quadrative amplitude modulation (QAM) .The numerical simulation shows this scheme with simple system design can obtain better security and it also can be applied in the wireless communication field

articleTitle: Adaptive Quantization for Interlaced Video Coding
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive quantization method by adjusting the rounding offset for scalar quantization adopted in AVS 1.0 part 2 zengqiang profile. The rounding offset is chosen adaptively based on minimum transform coefficients energy difference for quantization, and the transform coefficient energy difference is calculated by the sum of absolute distortion before quantization and after dequantization simply. The proposed adaptive quantization provides up to about 0.3 dB improvement for high bitrate application in terms of peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) based on public AVS reference software, with low computational complexity and memory consuming, especially for the interlaced video coding

articleTitle: An Adaptive Assistant-Aided Clustering Scheme for Mobile Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: For large mobile ad hoc networks, a cluster-based architecture can facilitate many services, such as routing selection and security management. In this paper, an adaptive clustering scheme in mobile ad hoc networks is proposed. The cluster head is chosen according to the connection degree and mobility of each node. Moreover, a cluster assistant is set inside each cluster to take charge part of duties of the cluster head and storage part of cluster information. Unlike other clustering algorithms, the diameter of clusters is adaptive and determined by the processing ability of cluster heads and member change frequency. During the runtime, clusters can split or merge according to member change frequency to maintain the cluster stable. Simulation results show that this clustering method is efficient and have a less change rate of cluster heads compared with some existing schemes

articleTitle: Multiuser Bit-Interleaved Space-Time-Frequency Coding System for Frequency Selective Block Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, we propose a phase-sweeping space-time-frequency bit interleaved coded modulation (PS-STF-BICM) scheme. By expanding the dimensions of sweeping matrix we achieve the correlation between the adjacent code matrices, and further time diversity is realized, and by further time diversity higher diversity gain is realized which effectively avoid possible burst errors in block fading channels. Also, the Singleton bound and BER performances are theoretically analyzed. Then we consider the downlink multiuser system model for PS-STF-BICM, the scheduling and capability of the three multi-access methods TDMA, F/TDMA and S/F/TDMA is analyzed. Through computer simulation results, we verify the system performance in frequency-selective block fading channels

articleTitle: A Source-Specific Multicast Routing Protocol for Mobile Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Multicast routing is a key technique to deploy multicast service in mobile ad hoc networks. This paper proposed a routing protocol ASSMR for source-specific multicast service in mobile ad hoc networks. A reverse path tree algorithm for delivery tree construction was designed for ASSMR, and novel delivery tree maintenance mechanisms dealing with dynamic situations were incorporated in ASSMR. Through detailed simulation experiments, the performance evaluation and comparison between ASSMR and ODMRP was presented

articleTitle: Structure and Performance of Space-Time Block Code
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper introduce the structure of STBC (space time block code) which is based on the crossing coding. First we introduce the Alamouti code, then we give the rules of the construct STBC. We also introduce the STTC in the 3GPP, which is the critical transmit diversity technology. After that we compare the performance of the different receive antennas and different modulation in the Rayleigh fading channel. From the simulation results we can draw the conclusions that the STBC could improve performance

articleTitle: A New Rate 3/4 Transmit Diversity for Five and Six Transmit Antennas with Phase Feedback
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: We present a rate 3/4 transmit diversity scheme for five or six transmit antennas. The new code provides a diversity order 4 and the same rate as quasi-orthogonal space-time block code (QOSTBC) which has a diversity order 3. Based on the perfect channel phase feedback (CPF) from the receiver to the transmitter, a precoding is employed at the transmitter to assure the acquirement of the full diversity. We also derive the closed-form expression for phase feedback, which is only the function of the channel gains known to the receiver. Moreover, decoding complexity is reduced by the partial linear and symbol-pair maximum likelihood (ML) decoding. Analyzing and simulation results confirm that the proposed transmit diversity scheme outperforms QOSTBC

articleTitle: 9Square: A New Architecture for MIMO WMN
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper presents a pipelined prototype for a planned 2.4 GHz wireless MIMO mesh network. The prototype design and channel allocation method are investigated in detail. MIMO's interference cancellation algorithm and MIMO-MU model are used to allow more parallel streams at one time, which greatly improves the throughput both for UDP and TCP transmission. The three non-overlapped channels are all used in this prototype. Channel 1 and 11 are assigned to backbones of mesh network and channel 6 is assigned to the connections between wireless clients and router. Simulation results by NS2 are analyzed at the end of this paper. Comparing with normal multi-channel-multi-interface mesh networks, the average throughput improves by more than 80% and 200%, while the packet delay is reduced by approximately 50% and 70% for 2-hop and 4-hop scenarios respectively

articleTitle: Processing Delay as a New Metric for On-Demand Mobile Ad Hoc Network Routing Path Selection
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A new metric, processing delay, has been proposed for route path selection. Processing delay, proposed by G. Bianchi, (2000) is used to calculate the performance of each node along the route. The function takes into account the number of active nodes in the vicinity of the forwarding node. Simulation experiments which have incorporated the new metric into the on-demand mobile ad hoc network protocol, dynamic source routing (DSR), have shown that the new metric has the characteristics of spreading the routes among the nodes in the network, thus minimizing congestion. The performance of the new on-demand ad hoc network, enhanced-DSR (eDSR), has shown a 20% reduction in packet delay, with marginal increase in hop counts

articleTitle: A Distributed Approach of WCA in Ad-Hoc Network
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a distributed approach of weighted clustering algorithms (WCA) which can be useful in enhancing the performance of clustering algorithms in mobile ad-hoc networks. In this distributed WCA, every node in the network collects the information of the nodes which are in its four hops range, computes a local clusterhead set using a GA approach, then the node which wins the most other node's support will be selected as the cluster head. After these, nodes nearby and the cluster head makes up a cluster. Simulation results show that the performance of distribute WCA is equivalent to the centralized WCA, but it is more adaptive to mobile ad-hoc networks

articleTitle: Simplified Iterative Symbol Timing and Carrier Phase Recovery Scheme for LDPC-Coded Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A simplified ML-based iterative synchronization scheme is proposed in this paper for LPDC-coded systems. Symbol timing and carrier phase are estimated in a simple way based on the maximum likelihood theory aided by hard decision obtained from LDPC decoder. The synchronized samples input to the decoder are updated when a new iterative estimation for symbol timing and carrier phase is completed. The synchronized samples are reconstructed by quadratic interpolation which is very simple and can be implemented in parallel. This approach is applied to a LDPC-coded QPSK system over AWGN channel. Simulation results demonstrate that the performance of the proposed scheme approaches that with the ideal synchronization

articleTitle: An Effective Method for PAPR Reduction in MC-DS-CDMA Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: As the combination of OFDM and CDMA, MC-DS-CDMA is a strong candidate for future wireless communication. However, challenges remain before it can achieve full potential. In this paper, we concentrated on reducing the peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) in MC-DS-CDMA system and proposed an effective method, which takes advantage of the characteristics of MC-DS-CDMA system. At transmitter, chips after time spreading are pseudo-random permuted firstly and clipping is exploited to reduce the PAPR. At receiver, the order of chips is recovered and the clipping noise is estimated and canceled. As a result, signal PAPR can be effectively controlled by clipping while avoid being severely distorted at some certain points by chip pseudo-random permutation at transmitter, and system performance loss caused by clipping can be mitigated to very little by canceling the clipping noise at receiver

articleTitle: A MVDR Multi-Code Receiver Based on Channel Estimation for HSDPA Mode
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: High speed downlink packet access (HSDPA) is one of the key features in the 3rd generation wireless communication standard for WCDMA. It is ongoing standardization effort to include a high data rate packet mode in the downlink direction, and is characterized by link adaptation using variable constellations (QPSK, 8PSK, 16QAM, 64QAM) and low spreading factor. The proposed MVDR multi-code receiver based on channel estimation is particularly adapted to HSDPA mode, and it gives a reasonable performance even in the case of high modulation order while keeping a lower complexity compare with LMMSE chip equalizer

articleTitle: Decision Directed Technique for Channel Estimation in OFDM Mobile Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A channel estimation method based on decision directed technique and pilot tracking for OFDM WLANS with mobile terminals is proposed in this paper. With the help of the decision symbols, the statistical characteristics of the transmitted data via the fading channel are applied for the channel estimation. And some reliable estimation results combined with pilot are used to track the change of the fading channel. The simulation results show that the proposed method has better performance than the channel estimation method based on training sequence or pilots

articleTitle: The Research and Practice of Mobile IP Position Management Based on Virtual Private Network
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Based on virtual private network technology, a method of IP mobile position management is presented. Each mobile agent (MA) is set up corresponding to a respective autonomy network on the Internet. Once MA is connected to the local ISP, a VPN that is used to manage the binding information of mobile nodal position is formed, which manages the position of mobile nodes. The memory structure of the binding information table and the algorithm used to manage the binding information of mobile position is designed. The simulative test shows that the design can solve the problem of triangular route, obtain an optimized route, and greatly increase the speed of receiving data compared with the standard mobile IP

articleTitle: MPEG-2 to AVS-M Transcoder with Mode Decision Optimization for Mobile Video Communication
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: AVS-M (the advanced audio video coding standard-mobile version) is established by Audio Video Standard Working Group of China for mobile-multimedia applications. To meet demands for communication between multimedia source and mobile system, transcoding from MPEG-2 to AVS-M is a key technique. However, the advanced intra and inter mode decision techniques adopted in AVS-M have a high computing requirement, which limits the real time implementation in mobile environment. In this paper, we propose a prediction mode decision optimization algorithm to reduce the transcoding complexity based on our previous work. Analyzing the relation among the prediction errors of blocks and doing adaptive motion re-estimation, we fast decide the best inter mode. Utilizing the directional feature of DCT coefficients, we fast decide the best intra mode. The simulation results show that the proposed MPEG-2 to AVS-M transcoder with mode decision optimization can be effectively adopted for mobile video communications

articleTitle: Iterative Detection of OFDM Signals in Dispersive Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper gives the ML and MMSE estimation of the time response of channel using pilot sequence and gives an iterative detection of transmitted signals using EM algorithm. A method of estimating the statistics of channel and operating noise power is also given, the simulation results show that MMSE method has good performance than ML, and the performance of the iterative detection is better when the number of the iteration increases. By using the estimation statistics of the channel and noise power, the performance can nearly approximate the perfect channel state information

articleTitle: A Joint Timing Recovery and SNR Estimation Algorithm for LDPC-Coded Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The effects of both symbol synchronization error and SNR estimation on the LDPC decoding performance have been investigated. Based on the statistical properties of the LDPC decoding output value, a joint timing recovery and SNR estimation algorithm is given, which puts the symbol synchronization, SNR estimation and iterative decoding together by two cooperative loops. After several iterative steps, the estimated values of symbol synchronization error and SNR convergent rapidly, and little performance degradation has been observed than the system with foregone SNR and accurate symbol timing

articleTitle: A Survey of Multicast Control in Mobile Internet
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Internet and mobile communication technologies make rapid developments in recent years and have great influence on people's life. Controllable multicast is a hot research filed in wired access network. Based on the controllable multicast model, this paper discussed the controllable multicast implementation scheme in mobile internet. Aimed at the two layer model multicast mobility protocol, host-view and mobicast, we provide the controllable multicast scheme based on mobile Internet

articleTitle: Multipath Performance for GNSS Signals Considering Correlation
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Code and carrier-phase multipath is still the important error sources in high-precision GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) applications, then a thorough understanding of code and carrier-phase multipath is the first step in the course of mitigating its impact in high precision applications. In virtually every study, however, the effects of autocorrelation function are neglected, and complete characterization of code and carrier-phase multipath error requires a fundamental theoretical description and mathematical modeling. Attention of this paper is focused primarily on the mathematical analysis on multipath error in terms of GNSS signals correlation function. The simulation results show a distinct change in the error envelope from that which has been derived previously using current GPS model for the autocorrelation function (ACF)

articleTitle: DCT-Based Speech Enhancement Using a New Speech Variance Estimation
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper proposes a new speech variance estimation algorithm for speech enhancement which operates in the discrete cosine transform (DCT) domain. The estimation method is based on the definition of variance and derived under the simple Gaussian distribution assumption for noise and speech components, which is in agreement with the DCT-based speech enhancement framework. The proposed method can be updated adaptively without making use of a weighting factor; it overcomes the disadvantage in the original algorithm that the trade off between the noise reduction and speech distortion brought into the signal can not be satisfied availably. A number of subjective and objective tests under various conditions show the improved performance of the proposed algorithm

articleTitle: Sub-Carrier Assignment for Multimedia Traffic Over OFDM Wireless Channel
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: With the rapid growth of wireless access to the Internet, there has been an increasing demand in providing high data rate real time traffic such as audio and video over wideband wireless channels. However, the transmitted multimedia traffic experience frequency-selective fading in wideband wireless channels. By dividing the wideband channel into several smaller sub-channels and sending multimedia traffic in parallel orthogonal sub-channels, which is widely known as orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), the frequency-selective channel can be transformed into a set of frequency-flat channels. OFDM has become a prospective technique for the next generation wireless communications. In this paper, we analyze the effect of sub-carrier assignment on the transmitted multimedia traffic. By increasing the number of sub-carriers, each sub-channel behaves practically as a quasi-static one, such that frequency-selective fading and intersymbol interference (ISI) can be alleviated. The multiplexing of sub-carriers is introduced to combat the variability of wireless channel, but the performance of wireless channel would also be degraded. We present a quality assessment of audio and video traffic over OFDM wireless channel based on sub-carrier assignment. Simulation results show that proper sub-carrier assignment could significantly reduce errors during high rate multimedia transmission

articleTitle: Web Services Matchmaking with Incremental Semantic Precision
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Semantic matchmaking plays an important role in Web services matchmaking. However, most proposed semantic matchmaking approaches in web services discovery were based on description logic (DL)'s subsumption reasoning, which had the deficiency of low precision. This paper first presented a simple and efficient semantic distance calculation method, then proposed a new Web services matchmaking approach with enhanced semantic precision based on this semantic distance calculation method. The enhanced matchmaking approach adopts the DL reasoner as the first filter to get the rough services set, then uses the semantic distance of concepts in domain ontology to refine the matchmaking result. To reduce the calculation complexity of matchmaking, the semantic distance calculation of concepts is guided by the result of semantic subsumption reasoning. The prototype and experiment show the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed approach

articleTitle: Outage Probability and Adaptive Power Allocation in Wireless Cooperative Communications
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, we develop an adaptive power allocation algorithm to minimize the outage probability in a two-hop single-relay wireless cooperative communication system under the average transmit power constraint. The adaptation is carried out in the time domain according to the channel state information (CSI), so a priori information of the channel is assumed. We analyze the outage performance in two different cooperation modes, i.e., amplify-and-forward (AF) and decode-and-forward (DF). We also study the impact of spectral efficiency and distance between nodes on outage performance. To facilitate the comparison, the outage performance of direct transmission is also analyzed as a baseline. Numerical results show that compared with fixed power allocation, adaptive power allocation has much better outage performance

articleTitle: An Improved Wireless Grid Security Infrastructure Based on Trusted Computing Technology
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Current grid computing has developed from traditional high performance, distributed and site-fixed computing to pervasive, ubiquitous and wireless computing. In practice, PKI-based solutions are introduced to solve security of grid computing. Because of limited computation power and limited memory spaces, it is difficult for wireless grid computing to gain secure solution in collaboration environment. The trusted computing (TC) technologies are introduced to offer great potential to improve this situation. In this paper, with treated trusted platform module (TPM) as a tamper-resistance module, a TC-enabled architecture is proposed to improve wireless grid security. Especially authorization protection is discussed to demonstrate how to gain enhanced and distributed security in grid environment

articleTitle: Peak-to-Average Power Ratio in WFMT Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper discuses the peak to average power ratio (PAR) for the signal of a novel wavelet based filtered multi-tone (WFMT) modulation. The wavelet based filtered multi-tone (WFMT) modulation was developed as an alternative line code for xDSL system and represents future extension of OFDM/DMT technologies. Because of the multicarrier nature of WFMT modulation, it is suitable for carrying high-speed data over a wide frequency band. The major drawback of the multicarrier system is the large PAR of the transmit signal, which causes the straightforward implementation to be costly and inefficient. In this paper, we examine the PAR of WFMT line code. A simple expression for PAR is developed, both for circular and for square constellation diagram of a QAM modulator. The results illustrate significant little peak-to-average power ratio of the WFMT transmit signal versus PAR in OFDM system

articleTitle: A Pre-Anticipated Handover Seamless QoS Scheme for IEEE 802.16e Based on Mobile Station Character Pattern
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Some character patterns of mobile station, such as conversation time and call times, obey the Pareto distribution. Based on this point, this paper proposes a pre-anticipated handover scheme to optimize the services for the dominant minority correspondent nodes, to offer better real-time applications and better QoS of TCP connections and to moderate package latency, especially in call initialization and handover processes. The scheme keeps dominant minority in the VIP address book and informs them of context messages on the handover, AAA, QoS, etc., before anticipated handover (so called address book informing scheme, or ABI), triggered by entering the border of cell. In case of signaling overflows, ERT-VR in IEEE 802.16e is introduced to forward the context messages, since IEEE 802.16e offers five QoS guarantees from the MAC layer. Performance simulations of the scheme show that delay and packet losses are reduced during call initialization and handover processes, and resource possession of RSVP are mitigated

articleTitle: Reduction of Out-of-Band Radiation in OFDM Based DRM Simulcast Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The simulcast transmission of the DRM and AM is an important approach during the interim from the analogue AM to digital AM broadcasting below 30 MHz. The reduction of out-of-band (OOB) radiation of OFDM signals in simulcast systems is one of the essential issues. In this paper, we introduce the concept of the cancellation carriers (CCs) which suppress the sidelobes of the OFDM signal by inserting well-defined subcarriers at the borders of the OFDM spectrum. In order to satisfy the demand of the simulcast system, we proposed limited-CCs method in which we occupy the subcarriers originally used for data transmission instead of inserting new subcarriers. Simulation results show that by the proposed technique the OOB power can be decreased by about 15 dB at the cost of a slight loss of data rate

articleTitle: Advanced MAC Protocol with Adjustable Sleep Mode for Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A great challenge of media access control design is brought by wireless sensor networks. Many schemes have been proposed, most of which are based on contention or TDMA. In this paper, we research on contention based MAC protocol for WSN, and present an advanced scheme with adjustable sleep mode based on T-MAC. The performance analysis show that the new scheme can further reduce the active time and the transmission latency

articleTitle: Robust Audio Coding Over Wireless Channels
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, a concatenated system combining turbo product codes and convolutional codes with soft decision Viterbi decoding algorithm and diversity is proposed to enhance the robustness of unequal error protection (UEP) scheme for wireless transmission of MPEG-4 advanced audio coding. The proposed scheme has been tested over the Gaussian and Rician fading channels. Under severe channels with random, burst and mixed bit error rates (BER) of 6.00 times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> and above, the proposed scheme provides a 90% improvement in residual BER performance, which is approximately 3 dB, with 19% increase in bandwidth over the original UEP scheme. At a high channel BER of 6.00 times 10 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>, the proposed scheme gives an error-free header frame. Compared with the concatenated convolutional codes, the proposed scheme provides 0.5 dB BER performance improvements with the same bandwidth. With diversity, the performance can be further improved by 3 dB at low SNR for the proposed scheme

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of a Novel Low-Density Parity-Check Coded Ultra Wide Band Impulse Radio (UWB-IR) System
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: As a new spread spectrum system, an ultra wide band technology has attracted much attention in high speed indoor multiple access radio communications. The conventional UWB system repeats and transmits pulses for each bit, but repeat code can't get code gains. As an error correcting code, low-density parity-check code (LDPC) has attracted much attention because of its good bit error performance. In this paper, we propose a novel LDPC coded direct-sequence ultra wide band (DS-UWB) system. Furthermore, we give the computer simulation and our results show that the LDPC coded UWB system can improve the BER over AWGN channel and IEEE 802.15.3a recommended UWB multi-path faded channel

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of High Rate Ultra-Wideband OFDM System between Two Different Modulation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The multi-band orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (MB-OFDM) scheme is a promising candidate proposal for the high rate ultra-wideband (UWB) wireless personal area networks (WPAN) (IEEE 802.15.3a) physical layer standard. Focusing on the system simulation and performance comparison between two different modulation techniques, we design a high rate MB-OFDM UWB system with convolutional code and run a complete simulation for such system. Simulation results show that QPSK modulation performs much better than 16QAM modulation and illustrate that the power consumption caused by inserting guard interval is about 1 dB. Especially, exploiting the convolutional code, the BER performance of MB-OFDM UWB system is improved greatly

articleTitle: Cyclic Correlation Based Symbol Duration Estimation for OFDM Signals
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper presents a novel method of symbol duration estimation for orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) signals. This method exploits the cyclostationarity of OFDM signals and estimates the symbol duration by maximizing a sum of modulus squares of cyclic correlation estimates in the cyclic domain. The computer simulation has been carried out and good performance has been obtained when the SNR is above 4 dB

articleTitle: Service Registration Model of Service Discovery Protocols in MANETs
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Service registration is an indispensable process of service discovery protocols in mobile ad hoc networks (MANETs). Due to lack of special analysis for service registration range, which is usually settled as a constant in traditional service discovery protocols, a node can not get any service information from its neighbor nodes when it starts a service request, sequentially it may not adapt to different network conditions. In this paper, we propose a destination-optimization service registration model based on different hop range through the analysis of source-not-assure problem. Moreover, we get the optimal result of the model which leads to the best communication quality. Finally we discuss results in three basic scenes: different possibilities of service request, different dynamic characters of topology and different ranges of network. Based on the analysis, we conclude how to enhance efficiency of service registration and performance of service discovery protocols in MANETs

articleTitle: Blind Multiuser Detection Algorithm for Asynchronous MFSK/FFH-MA System
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A MMSE-based blind multi-user detection algorithm for multilevel frequency shift keying/fast frequency hopping multiply access asynchronous communication system is proposed, detector implements blind detection without prior knowledge of address of co-channel interference users. The detector exploits energies of user signal and implement decisions through distinguish most sum row and its minimum mean square error (MMSE) of decode T-F matrix. The performance of proposed detector is analyzed and compared with other asynchronous multi-user detector. Simulation results show that the proposed asynchronous multi-user detector has a strong capability of resistant false alarm and deletion; meanwhile, it has low complication

articleTitle: Fast Frequency Offset Estimation Method for OFDM
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A fast frequency offset estimation scheme for OFDM is proposed. This scheme is low-overhead oriented, which uses only one OFDM symbol with L identical slots as preamble. By extracting the phase from correlation between two identical halves of the preamble, the fractional frequency offset is estimated and then compensated. After reshaping the compensated preamble into many L-point sub-symbols, which are processed by FFT algorithm, the estimate of integer frequency offset is accomplished by finding the maximum magnitude of the combined frequency domain signals. To further reduce the computational load of the algorithm, the scheme is carried out in a multistage manner. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme exhibits good performance, while maintaining a low complexity

articleTitle: Multiuser Transmission in Conjunction with Smart Antennas for the Downlink of TDD-CDMA System
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The multiuser transmission (MUT) is an effective way to eliminate the multiple-access interference (MAI) and the inter symbol interference (ISI) in the downlink channel of TDD-CDMA. In this paper, a novel MUT model is developed. In the model, the MUT combined with smart antennas (SA) is taken to improve the performance of TDD-CDMA in the spatial-temporal channel. Two different MUT algorithms in conjunction with the beamforming algorithm of SA are researched and the simulation results illustrate that the new MUT model achieves the better performance than the MUT model without SA

articleTitle: Fast-Convergence SMI Adaptive Beamforming Based on Frequency-to-Time Pilot Transform for OFDM System
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: We propose an adaptive beamforming scheme for the combination of orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) and adaptive antenna array.
