This mechanism can improve the precision of LEAST (loss estimation algorithms for TCP) and make CETEN more robust. The method shows efficiently in experiments that it can advance throughput by 14%-42% and decrease unnecessary retransmit near 2 times

articleTitle: A Novel Orthogonal Comb Spectrum Correlation Demodulation Method for the UWB Carrier Envelope Modulation
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Considering the frequency spectrum characteristics of the UWB carrier envelope modulation (CEM) scheme which was first introduced in ("The carrier envelope modulation (CEM) scheme for ultra-wideband WPAN communication", IEEE ISCIT 2005, vol.2, pp.837-841, 12-14 Oct. 2005), a novel orthogonal comb spectrum correlation demodulation method is presented in this paper. In order to satisfy the condition of orthogonal comb spectrum, the carrier frequency selection criteria is also derived. The performance analysis and simulation results not only show the feasibility of the new demodulation scheme, but also prove that it has the same performance as the demodulation method in time domain. Comparing with the comber filter demodulation scheme in time domain, the new demodulation scheme has simpler structure, and can be implemented by all digital circuits without RF comber filters

articleTitle: An Adaptive Space-Time Multiuser Detection Algorithm for CDMA Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Based on the minimum mean squared error (MMSE) between the data stream and the linear combiner output, a new multiuser detection (MUD) algorithm that combines space-time (ST) processing and antenna diversity on direct-sequence CDMA signals is proposed. The new ST-MUD algorithm does not require explicit estimation of channel and signaling information, as such it avoids any channel estimation error and provides robust and accurate results. An adaptive implementation of the new ST-MUD algorithm using training sequences is given and simulated. The new ST-MUD algorithm provides a performance better than that of existing algorithms and is especially suitable for CDMA systems

articleTitle: A Novel Blind Channel Estimation for Space-Time Coded OFDM on Time Varying Mobile Radio Channels
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A novel blind channel estimation scheme is presented for space-time coded OFDM (STC-OFDM) systems. This scheme obtains the channel estimates by exploiting the priori knowledge of the mapping constellation and the minimum leakage method, rather than the statistical properties of signals, and requires short data records especially for moderate and high SNRs, thus can achieve competitive performance in time varying channels. Simulation results comparing this scheme with a training-based scheme in time varying channels are presented

articleTitle: Performance of Ranging and Positioning Models with Impulse UWB
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The key concern of this paper is to study ranging and positioning algorithms based on the estimation of time of arrival (TOA) with impulse radio ultra wide band (IR-UWB) signal And the ranging and positioning models based on IR-UWB are established; the influences of different signal noise ratio (SNR) and different Gaussian derivative pulses on ranging and positioning are analyzed. Root mean squared error (RMSE) is used to scale the performance of the ranging and positioning. Performances of the ranging and positioning models are examined through simulation. With the increasing of SNR, the accuracy of ranging and positioning is higher. Furthermore, the higher order Gaussian pulse is advised to be exploited in order to improve the accuracy of range and position estimation

articleTitle: Convolutional Coding Quasi-Synchronous CDMA System Using Real-Valued Self-Orthogonal Finite-Length Sequences
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A set of real-valued self-orthogonal sequences of a zero correlation zone is applied to a variable rate quasi-synchronous CDMA system without interchannel interferences in a limited shift range. In each transmitter, the synchronizing sequence and the multi-rate data are convolved with the user sequence, and quantized to the integer signal. In a receiver, the synchronizing pulse and the data train are detected with suppressed distortions and interferences

articleTitle: Study on Blind Paths in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Random deployment of sensors may induce blind paths problem in wireless sensor network. To some applications of WSNs, the existence of blind paths will endanger the networks. It is necessary to study and solve the blind paths problem. In this paper, we examine the blind paths in wireless sensor networks and advance a feasible solution to it

articleTitle: A Fast Inductance Extraction Engine
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A fast inductance extraction engine is presented. With a fast multipole accelerated generalized minimal residual (GMRES) based three-dimensional (3-D) field solver, the software extracts parasitic inductance very quickly and accurately for interconnects with arbitrary geometries. The engine makes it possible the fast and highly-accurate analysis for critical nets in radio frequency (RF) application, antennae and even microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) devices. Moreover, the architecture of this engine is introduced, and some examples are given to demonstrate the extraction validity of the software which is presented

articleTitle: SCSR: A Novel MAC Protocol for Mobile Ad Hoc Network
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper presents a novel MAC protocol that employs combination of TDMA and power control schemes for ad hoc network. The collision resolution signaling protocol is modified and integrated in our protocol to eliminate the hidden terminals. The RTS/CTS handshake takes place at the maximum power to guarantee floor acquisition, while the SBT/DATA/ACK exchange takes place at the minimum power required for communication to realize parallelism in data transmission. The transmit power of sender is limited in order not to destroy the data transmission of the established sender-receiver pairs. The preliminary simulation results demonstrate that, with properly chosen parameters, our protocol works well and achieves considerably high throughput (near 290% of IEEE 802.11 in dense network) and acceptable

articleTitle: Comparative Investigation on MU-MIMO Schemes for TDD MIMO OFDMA Uplink
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: CSI can be utilized at the transmitter to implement close loop multiuser MIMO and obtain both full spatial multiplexing and multiuser diversity gain in uplink. In this paper, multiuser per antenna rate control (MU-PARC) and multiuser singular value decomposition (MU-SVD) for spatial division multiplexing (SDM) of MIMO OFDM are investigated and a novel joint spatial frequency proportional fairness (PF) scheduling is proposed to guarantee the user fairness. MU-SVD is expected to achieve better system throughput since it can achieve full transmission and reception diversity and multiuser diversity gain, while MU-PARC can only achieve reception diversity and multiuser diversity gain. From the simulation results, the throughput of MU-SVD is 31% higher than that of MU-PARC for 4times2 MIMO and 8times4 MIMO scenario when SNR at receiver antenna is set as 10 dB without path loss and shadowing

articleTitle: A Pairwise Ordered Successive Interference Cancellation Algorithm for VBLAST
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The classic detection algorithm of VBLAST, OSIC (ordered successive interference cancellation), is a good compromise between performance and complexity comparing to the optimum ML (maximum likelihood) algorithm. Due to the error propagation, the detection errors in the previous stages would degrade the accuracy of the forthcoming stages' detection and the overall performance of OSIC. We propose, in this paper, an POSIC (pairwise OSIC) algorithm aiming at reducing the errors in each detection stage and the numbers of the stages in the detection process to diminish the error propagation. Instead of detecting one substream in each stage, the POSIC algorithm using ML to jointly detect two strongest sub streams in each stage and then eliminate the contribution of the detected substreams from the received signals until all the transmitted substreams were detected

articleTitle: An Efficient Adaptive Decoding for Block Turbo Codes
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A novel adaptive threshold-decoding algorithm for block turbo codes (BTCs) was proposed. Simulations for a few combinations of BCH codes were carried out with the proposed algorithm and Chase algorithm for the purpose of comparison. The error correction performance with the suggested algorithm was negligibly degraded comparing with that using the Chase algorithm while it gained 1 dB at BER=10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> against Fragiacomo et al.'s results. Furthermore, the suggested algorithm reduced the number of codewords to be searched and speeded up the decoding process

articleTitle: A Reduced-Complexity Parallel Interference Cancellation/Decoding for Convolutionally Coded CDMA Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, parallel interference cancellation and decoding for convolutionally coded DS-CDMA systems is investigated. Firstly, we derive a reduced-complexity PIC/decoding (simplified PIC/decoding). Secondly, two forms of simplified PIC/decoding are analyzed, and compared with the exact PIC/decoding over Rayleigh fading channel. It shows that the simplified PIC/decoding achieves the performance close to the exact PIC/decoding if the tentative decisions of coded symbols are linearly computed in terms of the sum of initial a priori log-likelihood rate (LLR) and updated a priori LLR, while a significant performance loss will occur if the tentative decisions of coded symbols are linearly computed in terms of the updated a priori LLR only. Besides, we compare the simplified PIC/decoding with matched-filter (MF) receiver and conventional PIC/decoding, which shows that the simplified PIC/decoding dominantly outperforms the MF receiver and conventional PIC/decoding. From these results we conclude that the proposed simplified PIC/decoding exhibits a favorable performance/complexity trade-off and is therefore more suitable for future practical application

articleTitle: On Capacity of Multiple Antenna LS-CDMA System in Ricean Fading Channel
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: We considered the effects of Ricean fading and suboptimum multicode detector on capacity of MIMO LS-CDMA system. Suboptimal multicode detector's behavior is very different in different Ricean channels and the loss of capacity incurred by it is also different. When Ricean channel is friendly, performance of suboptimal multicode detector can approach that of optimal multicode detector rapidly as K-factor increases. On the other side, the loss of capacity incurred by suboptimal detector is huge when K-factor increases. This result gives guideline in the development of practical wideband MIMO-CDMA system based on LS code

articleTitle: The Scheme Design and Implementation of the Baseband Part of a Wireless OFDM System
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: OFDM is the key technique in the next generation communication. In this paper, the design and implementation scheme of the baseband part of multimedia communication system carried by automobile is described. It is developed with the COFDM technique and MPEG-4 standard. The baseband system is mainly composed of two boards-source and channel encoders/decoders, which include some sub-blocks for different functions. The equipment designed can transmit audio/video signals at a wireless mobile channel for some special users exclusively. Based on the theory of software defined radio and the idea of modular function design, it is implemented by the universal high performance chips-DSP, FPGA and EPLD. It supplies a convenient user interface and the software embedded in the chips can be programmed to different functions. So it is easy to debug and modify for designers with a much lower cost

articleTitle: Design and Evaluation of Strategies for Full Mobility Provision in Bluetooth Wireless Personal Area Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The rapid development of services requiring full mobility imposes the need of new network topologies and strategies in order to support efficient management of connections being transferred between picocells. The goal of this paper is to propose and evaluate several alternatives for Bluetooth based wireless personal area networks to achieve full mobility features for mobile terminals operating over them

articleTitle: Error and Rate Joint Control for Wireless Video Streaming
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, a precise error-tracking scheme for robust transmission of real-time video streaming over wireless IP network is presented. By utilizing negative acknowledgements from feedback channel, the encoder can precisely calculate and track the propagated errors by examining the backward motion dependency. With this precise tracking, the error-propagation effects can be terminated completely by INTRA refreshing the affected macroblocks. In addition, due to lots of INTRA macroblocks refresh will entail a large increase of the output bit rate of a video encoder, several bit rate reduction techniques are proposed. They can be jointly used with INTRA refresh scheme to obtain uniform video quality performance instead of only changing the quantization scale. The simulations show that both control strategies yield significant video quality improvements in error-prone environments

articleTitle: Compensation of Phase Jitter in Frequency Hopped OFDM Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The phase jitter of frequency hopped OFDM systems (FH-OFDM) is very different from that of OFDM systems working on a constant radio frequency (RF). In this paper the SNR loss is analyzed for the system ruined by the phase jitter. Based on the analysis on the frequency domain specification of phase jitter signal, a phase jitter compensation (PJC) algorithm is presented based on the design principle of inverse filter for FH-OFDM. Least square (LS) approach is used to exploit the phase jitter information existing in the scattered pilots. Analysis and simulation results show that choosing an appropriate length for the filter the algorithm can improve the BER performance effectively with low complexity, which will not reduce the system bandwidth availability

articleTitle: Secure Anonymous Threshold Subliminal Channel for Ad Hoc Environments
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The (t, n) threshold cryptography is an important method for sharing a group secret message in dynamic groups such as ad hoc groups. Using subliminal channel, one can send a secret message to an authorized receiver and the message cannot be discovered by any unauthorized receivers; it satisfies different requirements of different kind of users. We discussed the security of HCW scheme and proposed a secure anonymous threshold subliminal channel. The proposed scheme has not any setup phase and allows mixture use of discrete-logarithm-type keys and RSA-type keys. Furthermore, the proposed scheme only has a simple initialization phase, thus, it is flexible and suitable for ad hoc environments. The new scheme can resist forgery and conspiracy attacks; the subliminal message sender is indistinguishable to others except the authorized users. Performance analysis and experiments show that the new scheme is more efficient in general

articleTitle: The On-Line Prediction of Self-Similar Traffic Based on Chaos Theory
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, we employ chaotic predictive technique to predict the self-similar traffic. Our novel method combines the algorithm of embedding window with the conception of independently determining embedding parameters. The algorithm we adopt for computing Lyapunov exponent has high computational efficiency. It can be implemented for on-line prediction, and applied in the resource management of wireless networks

articleTitle: Time-Frequency Double Differential Encoding and Detection in Cyclic Prefix Assisted CDMA System
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Considering the correlation of channel impulse response (CIR) between two neighboring data blocks in time domain and two adjacent subcarriers in frequency domain, a novel time-frequency double differential encoding scheme is proposed for cyclic prefix assisted CDMA system, and corresponding non-coherent equalization and detection receiver based on minimum mean square error (MMSE) criterion is presented. Computer simulation results show that the proposed method outperforms conventional differential encoding method in fast fading channels and multiuser systems

articleTitle: Wireless Sensor Network Autonomic Agent Based on In-Cluster Directional Evidence Reasoning
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The sensor nodes performance evaluation and uncertainty reasoning are vital to dynamic, fault tolerance wireless sensor network management. An efficient directional evidence reasoning algorithm is put forward based on in-cluster directional hierarchical architecture, which is adapted to capture epistemic uncertainty in sensor-network. Accounting for NP complete of combination of Dempster Shafer theory (DST) for central algorithm, one distribute in-cluster algorithm is applied with fast Mobius transform (FMT) based on coarsening combination of evidences. This method not only offers an efficient framework for uncertainty reasoning with low computation cost, but also balances energy budget between ubiquitous computation and communication. Simulation verified it efficiency for self-management, and lifetime of wireless sensor network is prolonged obviously

articleTitle: Low Complexity Adaptive Group Detection in Layered Space-Time MIMO Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: It discusses the detection techniques of the LAST (also known as the vertical Bell Laboratories layered space-time (V-BLAST) scheme) for both single user (SU) and multiuser(MU) MIMO wireless communication systems. To strike a better tradeoff between computational complexity and performance, a simple, yet effective group detection with adaptive group order successive interference cancellation (AGOSIC) is addressed. The new approach sequentially peels off the detected signals group by group in a descending order of power levels, and, most noticeable, the number of users in each group are adaptively determined based on the average of the post signal to noise ratio (SNR) to achieve a better ordering of signals. More specifically, according to the threshold, which is stage dependent, the remaining signals in each stage are partitioned into two groups: the desired group and the residual group. After conducting the layered space-time processing scheme, the signals in the desired group, whose SNRs are all greater than or equal to the threshold, are then removed. The whole process is repeated until all users are detected. The new scheme can suppress the effect of multiple access interference (MAI) in the MU-MIMO, and adaptively mitigate the effect of multiple access interferences (MSI) in both SU-MIMO and MU-MIMO. Simulations show that proposed scheme in both scenarios can yield close and sometime even better than, bit error rate (BER) performance as that of the previous works, but with substantially reduced complexity and latency

articleTitle: A Scalable Wideband Speech Coder for Mobile Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Achieving effective voice communication over mobile ad hoc networks (MANETs) offers both new challenges and opportunities for speech coding. This paper investigates a new 13.6 kb/s subband structure bandwidth scalable (SB-SWS) scheme for MANETs, which is based on a high-quality narrowband speech coder, the 11.8 kb/s G.729 Annex E, with the higher band using a bandwidth extension (BWE) approach to reduce bit rate required. The performance of the scalable coder is tested for MANETs with a simulation test. The results demonstrate that the scalable approach contributes to effective and reliable voice communication in MANETs

articleTitle: Distributed Internet Telephony System Using a Novel P2P Architecture
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Recent years, research on Internet telephony technology based on unstructured or structured peer-to-peer (P2P) networks has been developed rapidly. In such systems, the routing efficiency and their scalability are challenging two problems. The structured networks have rigorous restriction to search condition, and rely on rigorous network topology. The unstructured networks avoid the limitations of centralized systems but their search algorithms are usually based on simple flooding schemes, showing server inefficiencies. In order to address these major limitations, this paper considers the characters of users in Internet telephony systems adequately, presents a novel P2P overlay network based on unstructured P2P networks, called self-organizing multi-character overlay (SOMCO), which adopts small-world network to construct the topology, and presents the corresponding routing algorithm for the system. In our simulation, compared with existing P2P Internet telephony system, SOMCO is much better on the routing efficiency and network scalability

articleTitle: The Novel Super-FEC Coding Scheme Based on the Block Turbo Code for Long-Haul Optical Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A novel super forward error correction (super-FEC) coding scheme (viz: the BTC code pattern of BCH(64,57) times BCH(64,57)) based on the block turbo code (BTC) in long-haul optical transmission systems is proposed in this paper. The BTC of Bose-Chaudhur-Hocguenghem (BCH)(64,57)timesBCH(64,57) has been constructed, simulated and analyzed. The simulation results and the performance analyses show that the net coding gain (NCG) of BCH(64,57)timesBCH(64,57) code at the sixth iteration is 0.35 dB more than that of Reed-Solomon (RS)(255,239) + convolutional self orthogonal code (CSOC) (k0/n0=6/7, J=8) code in ITU-T G.975.1 at the third iteration for a BER of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-12</sup> and the novel BTC has the advantageous characteristics such as the shorter component code and the rapid encoding/decoding speed, these advantages reduce not only the complexity for implementing the software/hardware but also the time delay for the encoding/decoding. Therefore, the novel BTC coding scheme can be used in large capacity, high-speed and ultra long-haul optical transmission systems. At last, the design and implementation of the novel BTC are also discussed

articleTitle: Bit Error Rate Analysis of CDMA Receiver with Linear and Circular Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The suitable use of array antennas in CDMA systems results in improvement in signal to interference ratio (SIR) and thus reducing bit error rate (BER). In general, SIR depends on the array configuration and is a function of the direction of the desired user and interferers. Here, the BER performance in linear multiuser detectors with use of linear and circular arrays is analysed and compared

articleTitle: The Multi-Level Mapping Sequential Gaussian Approximation for MIMO Detection
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper presents a low complexity detection scheme, based on sequential Gaussian Approximation, called multi-level mapping SGA detection, for multi-input multi-output wireless communication systems with high-order QAM modulation. In the SGA detection, only part of transmit symbol combinations contributing significantly to posterior probabilities are retained, having a complexity linear with retained branches number. Due to the property of high-order QAM formats, the new scheme calculates the sequence weight in step of two bits, resulting in a complexity reduction from exponential in the modulation order to linear, compared to basic SGA detection. Simulation results show that the multi-level mapping SGA can provide near the performance of the basic SGA detection

articleTitle: A Partial MRT Algorithm for Closed-Loop Spatial Multiplexing Systems with Transmit Antenna Selection
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The paper investigates closed-loop spatial multiplexing systems with transmit antenna selection. Since the bandwidth limit of feedback channel, a partial MRT algorithm is proposed to reduce the amount of feedback information. An improved water-filling power allocation algorithm is obtained for optimal power allocation. The proposed method can not only reduce the amount of feedback, but also fully exploit potential multiplexing capability of the channel. Simulation results show that transmit antenna selection can compensate the loss caused by imperfect CSI at the transmitter

articleTitle: A Lightweight Multi-Source IP Multicast Protocol
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper introduces LMSM, a novel lightweight multi-source IP multicast protocol. After being aware of a specific source for a many-to-many group, the hosts, including the mobile ones, initiate their JOIN/REQS/LEAVE messages towards the source, and a hybrid multi-source-multi-receiver tree for multi-party group communication is formed. Non-LMSM routers are bypassed by tunnels, which eliminates the dependence on multicast-specific routing. Analyses show that LMSM is scalable and the host, even a mobile host, can take part in the group communication easily

articleTitle: Handoff in Virtual Cell System Based on Distributed Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Legacy cellular infrastructure can not fulfill the requirements introduced by space time code (STC), joint transmission (JT), MIMO and other wireless technologies. We propose a novel virtual cell structure based on distributed antenna, which decreases the handoff frequency and allows access via WLAN randomly. In this paper, we emphasis on construction and selection of the virtual cell, and describe the horizontal adaptive handoff procedure in the architecture. To support vertical handoff between cellular and WLAN, VHTN and VHSN were introduced into the architecture. Mathematics analysis shows that the system promotes the performance in delay and packet loss

articleTitle: Adaptive Fast Inter Mode Decision for Wireless Video Applications Using H.264/AVC
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, we proposed an adaptive fast inter mode decision algorithm to reduce the computation complexity of H.264/AVC encoder. It makes use of spatio-temporal correlation to filter out unlikely modes. Instead of performing all the seven inter prediction modes, only part of them are chosen for motion estimation and rate distortion optimization (RDO) procedure. Adopting a dynamic adjusted threshold makes the proposed method work well in different bit-rate conditions, especially in low bit-rate. Experimental results indicate that the proposed algorithm can achieve 23% time saving in inter mode decision on average while maintaining the similar rate distortion performance

articleTitle: Coordination Mechanisms for Selfish Routing in Multi-Channel Wireless Mesh Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In selfish routing, k transmissions are managed by k different agents. All the agents are selfish; their goals are to minimize their own costs without considering the overall performance of the network. Meanwhile, the agents are rational, they always meet the embarrassment that whether they face the probability of causing interference for routing flow by a short cut or they route flow by a longer way steadily. We introduce the game theoretic tools to direct the agents to make feasible choices and the coordination mechanism to improve the system performance which has been deteriorated for the lack of coordination. We yield a sufficient condition of the existence of pure strategy Nash equilibria and proof it in this paper. Some simulations reveal the feasibility of our proposition

articleTitle: Offline Text Message Storage and Recovery Based on Inverted Files in Peer-to-Peer Internet Telephony
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Offline text message based on inverted files provide some new extensible service for the user, which lets the user search in all offline messages to get a satisfied result. Moreover, the message is recovered quickly from the inverted files and resent to the user. The scattered original messages need not be reserved after indexing, so the storage space can be saved in the system. This paper discusses the function of inverted index compression, similarity query process and message recovery with block processing in a high efficiency system. The experiments of simple prototype system validate our analytical methods

articleTitle: Design of Media Gateway Controller in 3G Softswitch
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: MGCP is a very important protocol in SG, and the quality of design of MGC has a critical impact on the performance of 3G core network, this paper studies the mechanism of MGCP, and proposes a design scheme of MGC, according to our analysis, we propose an implementation prototype of MGC

articleTitle: A Robust Superimposed Pilot Scheme in MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, a novel superimposed pilot scheme is presented, which not only has the optimized MSE (mean squared error) of channel estimation, SINR (signal-to-interference noise ratio) and PAPR (peak-to-aver age power ratio) simultaneously, but also is robust to de-offset. The relationships of MSE and SINR with pilot parameters are analyzed through simulation. Comparison proves that the proposed pilot scheme has both high SINR and good robustness

articleTitle: Effects of Imperfect Channel State Information on the Performance of Adaptive MIMO-OFDM Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Adaptive multiple input multiple output (MIMO) orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems have a great potential to increase the performance when the channel state information (CSI) is accurately known at transmitter (TX) side. However, the perfect CSI is a too strong assumption for a wireless system operating. This paper presents a low complexity adaptive MIMO OFDM systems which takes into account estimated CSI errors and channel correlation at TX side. By analyzing the equivalent signal noise rate (SNR) and spatial multiplexing (SM) patterns, we evaluate the effects of estimated CSI errors and channel correlation at TX side on the performance of adaptive MIMO-OFDM systems. The simulation results clearly show the performance comparison of adaptive MIMO-OFDM systems between perfect CSI and imperfect CSI

articleTitle: An Effective Integration of Hierarchical Cellular and Hierarchical Mobile MPLS
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, according to hierarchical mobile MPLS (H-MPLS) and mobile IP network based on hierarchical MPLS (MINHM), we propose an Effective Integration of hierarchical cellular and hierarchical mobile MPLS (EIHCHMM) that integrates the wireless cell and wired MPLS. The scheme is valuable because it decreases the end-to-end delay but it doesn't affect the throughput. The evaluation results show that the idea of EIHCHMM is correct

articleTitle: A Hybrid Technique Based on RS Coding and Least Square Method for Clipping Distortion Mitigation in OFDM System
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) signal has a large peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR). Hence, several techniques have been proposed to reduce the PAPR. Clipping is a widely used technique to reduce the peak amplitudes by nonlinearly distorting the OFDM signal at or around the peaks. However, clipping results in symbol distortion because of the nonlinearly operation to the signal peak value. Recently, a DFT-based method for OFDM system to compensate for the performance degradation has been proposed. In this paper, we investigate the hybrid method which consists of RS coding and least square method. Through computer simulation, our results show that the hybrid method is an effective technique to mitigate the clipping distortion

articleTitle: On the Performance of Multi-Node Generalized Selection Cooperative System with Minimum Selection
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper proposes a multi-node generalized selection cooperative system with minimum selection for multi-hop wireless networks. The close-form expressions of the regenerative outage probability are derived and analyzed over Rayleigh fading channels. The numerical and simulation results show that proposed system achieves a good tradeoff between the system performance and the process capability of the destination node, and it is very helpful to reduce the power consumption and the hardware complexity of the destination node without losing the required performance

articleTitle: Implementing Context-Aware Computing in 802.11 LAN
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Context-aware computing is emerging as a promising technology for mobile and pervasive environments. Unfortunately, complex context-aware applications are still hard to build. In this paper, we describe an 802.11 based indoor context-aware system used in hospital. Our objective is to empower mobile devices to recognize the context in which hospital workers perform their tasks. This system is an accessory of the management system in the hospital, and it can add Context-aware ability to the existing system by providing Context-aware communications. In our work, we use BAFO (Be Away From Obstacles) algorithm to deploy APs (Access Points), and use a Received Signal Strength (RSS) based Algorithm MNNSS (Modified Nearest Neighbor in Signal Space) to position mobile terminals, then describe the implementation of this multi-agent based system

articleTitle: A Genetic Algorithm for Evolutionary Voting System
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Different from traditional fault tolerant systems (e.g. the voting system), genetic algorithms are applied to the actual hardware systems, which ensures that the units found to be faulty could be improved and eventually reach full functionality through evolution. We design and implement a genetic algorithm by C++ language in the evolutionary voting system. Experimental results shows a genetic algorithm to be an effective strategy in some areas of engineering optimization

articleTitle: Combinatorial Construction of Low-Density Parity-Check Codes for Short Block Length and High Rate Applications
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper presents a method to construct regular low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes of short block length and high rate based on a special type of combinatoric designs, i.e., balanced incomplete block designs (BIBDs) with lambda = 2 whose construction are based on cyclic difference families. Although the Tanner graph of the codes constructed contains some cycles of length 4, simulation results show that they perform well under belief propagation (BP) decoding. Further, these codes are quasi-cyclic (QC) codes and hence can be encoded efficiently

articleTitle: A Fair Anonymous Multicast Fingerprinting Scheme
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Today, much multicast fingerprint schemes have been proposed to protect the digital content's copyright in multicast environment. All of those schemes only consider the distributor's right. The generation and the embedding of the fingerprint are controlled by the distributors. Since that, the accusation against the charged redistributor, who was the subscriber in some earlier transaction, is rejected because that the distributor can also get the distributed fingerprinted copy to this subscriber. This is known as the subscriber's right problem. In Emmanuel and Kankanhalli 2003, they propose a scheme to protect both the distributor's copyright and subscriber's rights for digital video multicast. But in their scheme, they never consider the unbinding problem and the privacy of the subscriber. In this paper, we proposed an anonymous multicast fingerprinting scheme, to fix the Emmanuel and Kankanhalli's scheme by solving the unbinding problem, protecting the subscriber's privacy through a trusted third party. The result is a security, fair and anonymous multicast fingerprint protocol

articleTitle: Consideration of Pre-Filter Bandwidth Optimization for Non-Coherent UWB Receiver
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Non-coherent receivers are attractive for pulsed UWB systems due to the implementation simplicity. However, it is subject to non-trivial performance degradation due to undesired noise enhancement, especially when the system configuration is inappropriate. This paper mainly concerns the pre-filter bandwidth optimization of the non-coherent receiver. The BER performance expression is derived, and an empirical criterion for pre-filter bandwidth selection is proposed based on corresponding numerical analyses

articleTitle: Cyclic Space-Time Block Codes and Decoding Algorithm in MIMO CDMA System
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A novel space-time coding scheme called cyclic space-time block coding (C-STBC) in MIMO CDMA system is presented. In the C-STBC scheme, the input symbols are split in blocks, each block has M symbols (M is the number of transmitting antennas), the M symbols are circularly encoded into M groups (each group has M cyclic symbols), the encoded M times M symbols are transmitted in M symbol durations through M antennas by multiplying M spread-codes respectively. A blind decoding algorithm for the C-STBC is also presented. Simulation results show that the proposed C-STBC is superior to the conventional STBC in MMO CDMA system

articleTitle: A Novel Simple DOA Estimation Algorithm Based on Direct Data Domain Approach Using Phase-Only Conjugate Gradient Method
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Recently, a direct data domain least square (D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>LS) approach has been developed so quickly for array signal processing in mobile communication and radar application. With D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>LS approach, only a single data snapshot is required, instead of multiple snapshots needed to form a covariance matrix in conventional algorithms. Moreover, The phase-only algorithms are so attractive due to the advantage on simple hardware implementation. Therefore, this paper proposes a novel simple direction of arrival (DOA) estimation algorithm based on D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>LS approach using phase-only conjugate gradient (CG) method. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can estimate the DOAs of signals accurately and deal well with coherent signals

articleTitle: Fast Algorithm for Sub-Pixel Motion Estimation Using Parabola Model for H.264/MPEG4 AVC
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, a fast sub-pixel motion estimation algorithm is presented for H.264/MPEG4 AVC video coding. The proposed methods are based on mathematical models of the motion compensated error distribution function to predict the possible searching direction. Here we do not select the parabola in the horizontal direction but the paraboloid in two dimension by five integer-pixels, the parabola can more exactly describe the moving and texture characteristic in the compressed pictures without strict limitation on the very low bit rate coding. In order to decide the coefficients of the paraboloid model which is suitable for most of sequences, the minimum mean square error (MMSE) from the best integer-pixel motion vector and its horizontally adjacent two half-pixel motion vectors are computed, then the MMSE correlation among three elements are compared and analyzed respectively. By an accurate modeling, we can effectively predict the further searching mode instead of full search. For the quarter-pixel accuracy motion vector, an approximation method is used to get the results from the half-pixel middle results directly. Experimental results show that the proposed method reduces the computational complexity down to 54% averagely, similar performance compared with other fast algorithms in speed, and degradation in the reconstructed video quality is negligible. At the same time, our proposed method does not depend on the integer-pixel searching mode

articleTitle: Numerical Study on the Average Noise Factor of LNA for UWB Impulse Radio Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Noise factor (NF) is used to quantify the degradation of the signal passing through RF circuits. The spot NF widely used in narrow band low-noise amplifier (LNA) is frequency dependent. It's necessary to redefine the NF for the wideband LNA where the ultra-wideband (UWB) signal pulse is assumed to be of the Gaussian pulse. The average NF suitable for the wideband LNA is discussed firstly. Numerical study on the average NF of LNA for UWB impulse radio is presented in this paper. The average NF is analyzed to quantify the relationship between LNA and Gaussian pulse. A design strategy is suggested that the Gaussian pulse frequency response is optimized to lower average NF. The average NF is equivalent to the spot NF when narrow band assumption is made. For wideband systems with constant frequency response, the average NF is determined by two endpoints frequency summation

articleTitle: Multi-Path Combining Scheme for ISI Suppression in DS-UWB Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Ultra Wide-band (UWB) recently attracts much attention as an indoor short range high-speed wireless communication technology for next generation networks. Direct sequence spread ultra wide-band (DS-UWB) systems uses extremely short pulses and has the advantage of high path resolution and can get multi-path diversity if using rake structured receivers such as selective rake (S-rake) receiver. Unfortunately inter-symbol interference (ISI) will become a significant performance limitation when data rate is high. Several techniques such as rake receiver using minimum mean square error (MMSE) combining weights and frequency domain equalization (FDE) have been proposed to combat ISI. Different from these relatively complex methods, a practical multi-path combining scheme (MPC) to suppress ISI in DS-UWB systems is proposed in this paper. Simulation results show that our proposal outperforms the conventional S-rake receiver especially in a high signal to noise ratio (SNR) scenario

articleTitle: On the MIMO Channel Capacity Saturation for Spatially Constrained Multielement Antenna Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In MIMO wireless communication systems, when more and more antennas are packed into a limited space, the antenna saturation phenomenon will appear. Moreover, the electromagnetic interactions among antennas will also become stronger and stronger and affect the antenna saturation effect considerably. Despite this, few studies consider these two effects jointly. Here, the effects of antenna saturation and mutual coupling are investigated jointly, thus a more practical result can be obtained

articleTitle: A Novel Framework for QoS Enhancement in Ad Hoc Network
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: We propose a novel network framework to support QoS in mobile ad hoc networks. The framework adopts a cross-layer mechanism including two aspects. 1) Virtual multi-queue of MAC layer can be schedules and managed according to the priority and routing hop numbers of high layer packets. 2) The network layer avoids routing breakage according to link lifetime and queue load information of neighbor nodes gathered by the MAC layer. The simulation results show that the network framework can reduce high priority packet delay and improve the network performance

articleTitle: A Data Synchronization Mechanism for Cache on Mobile Client
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Cache technology was an important technique that supported the disconnected operation between mobile clients and servers. For the time being, the research on mobile client cache data maintenance and that of the synchronization between mobile client and server were relatively independent of each other i.e. rarely where the two were combined for putting into practice. This article combines these two kinds of key techniques organically. It proposes that every data item entering the cache has priority property and data type property, and proceeds data collection under a consistent state and also updates, replaces the cache according to the result set of mobile client transaction. This article puts forward a kind of synchronous mechanism based on mobile client cache data classification, adopting different synchronous strategy for different data and so raises the efficiency of mobile database system and the success ratio of committing transient transaction

articleTitle: Bandwidth Aware Cache Invalidation in Error Prone Wireless Mobile Environments
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The IR-UIR based approach for cache invalidation is an attractive solution for reducing the query delay where data changes frequently. However, it achieves this by increasing the frequency of replication resulting in consumption of large amount of bandwidth. Bit sequencing approach proposed to address the problem of long disconnection cannot be used in this scenario as even a single bit error would collapse the entire hierarchy and also the UIRs are very short reports, which contain very less data items. In this paper, we propose to use hashing techniques to represent the data items so as to reduce the bandwidth requirements. Using hashing we divide the data items into different groups called buckets. By using the hash key of a bucket the data items in that bucket are represented using less number of bits than is actually required. Since data items are to be accompanied by the time at which they are modified, we reduce the number of bits required to represent time by using the amount of time elapsed since the data item is modified. Detailed mathematical analysis and simulation experiments are carried out to evaluate the proposed methodology. Compared to the previous methods our solution not only requires less bandwidth but also performs well in erroneous environments

articleTitle: Turbo Multiuser Receiver for Rayleigh Flat Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, the iterative multiuser receiver is explored over the Rayleigh flat fading channel. The work is based on both the turbo principle and parallel interference cancellation (PIC). Together with PIC, the turbo decoder, in view of its powerful error-correction ability, pushes the convergence of the whole receiver. In SIMO system the simulation results show a significant improvement using the diversity receiver over the single antenna system

articleTitle: Adaptive Subcarrier and Antenna Allocation for Multiuser MIMO-OFDM Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Subcarrier and antenna allocation is one of most important issue for multiuser MIMO-OFDM systems radio resource management. In this paper, a suboptimal subcarrier and antenna allocation algorithm with less complexity is proposed, based on the analysis of optimal antenna and subcarrier allocation algorithm. Numerical results show that there is only a little performance deterioration on capacity upper bound with the proposed algorithm compare to optimal algorithm, and multiuser diversity is also exploited simultaneously by the allocation algorithm in multiuser environment

articleTitle: A QoS Pre-Configure Mechanism on DiffServ Mobile IPv6 Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: IPv6 is the next generation IP protocol to solve the lack of IP address problem and it has been widely used on Internet. The future wireless network would be based on IPv6 to provide services for more users. Mobile IPv6 is proposed to remain a device reachable even when the device roams away from one network to another on single-hop wireless networks. Mobile IPv6 is a best-effort services model and QoS solutions for real-time mobile applications are needed. A QoS pre-configure mechanism (QoSPCM) is contributed to guarantee quality of service (QoS) on DiffServ based mobile IPv6 networks. SIP is extended to perform AAA processes and distribute QoS parameters. QoSPCM uses differentiated service (DiffServ) to guarantee QoS on wired backbone. Roaming users can keep communications with QoS guaranteed right after it performed handover. Voice software and DiffServ mobile IPv6 test-bed are implemented to demonstrate the validity of QoSPCM. Experiment results shown that it is necessary to guarantee QoS for real-time applications on crowded networks, and mobile user could get the same QoS guaranteed after it performed handover on QoSPCM

articleTitle: Performance Tests and Application Strategies of Spatial Indexes in the Embedded-GIS Data Management
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Spatial indexes arranged by some sequence, are related to the positions, shapes of geographic entities and relations among them, which describe the outline info of object identifier (OID), minimum bounding rectangle (MBR) and pointers to storage location. Usually, the index situated between the spatial operating algorithms and the entities, enhances the efficiency of spatial operations by filtering and erasing irrelevant ones. Especially, for resource-constrained mobile terminals with embedded-GIS, it's necessary to establish proper index strategies to solve the problem of limited memories conflicting with enormous data and the requirement of real-time processing. The paper not only stated the design and realization of the Seq-list, KD-tree, quad-tree and R-tree indexes carried on embedded-GIS, but also applied these to Compaq iPAQ H3800 conducting massive careful tests. Based on analyzing and contrasting test results of memories occupied, time spent and power consumed, the paper appraised the validity of above indexes and proposed corresponding strategies for different embedded-GIS application environments

articleTitle: An Efficient Architecture for Wideband Digital Down Conversion Based on the Goertzel Filter
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: An efficient architecture for wideband digital down conversion (DDC) is presented. The basic idea is to decimate the input signal prior to filtering, and then realize the mixing process by the use of the Goertzel filter. Compared with the conventional wideband DDC structure, computational complexity with the proposed structure is only 1/M as much when decimation factor is M. Furthermore, this structure eliminates the constraint on the tuning frequency of mixer in the conventional efficient structure based on the polyphase filter. Simulation results are presented to illustrate the validity of new structure

articleTitle: Detection and Localization of Transmission Error in MPEG-4 Video
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The growth in mobile communication and Internet usage has lead to increase in demand for robust transmission of compressed video over error prone channels. The quality of decoded video in erroneous environments depends on efficient detection, localization and concealment of errors. In fact, the role of error detection and localization is very important because undetected erroneous macroblocks (MBs) are not concealed and correct MBs may be termed as erroneous. However, traditional error detection method isn't enough for detection. A novel detection method proposed recently can detect some special errors, but can't make precise localization. In this paper, an improved error detection and localization technique using syntactic, semantic and statistical information in MPEG-4 is proposed. This scheme can detect most types of transmission error and locate the exact position of the first error. Experimental results show the proposed technique can achieve high error detection ratio, usually more than 90%, and increase the decoded video quality efficiently

articleTitle: Simulation-Based Performance Analysis of Dynamic Channel Scheduling Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Wireless personal area network (WPAN) has gained a lot of attention in industry recently. Ultra-wideband (UWB) presents itself as a good alternative physical layer of WPAN, for both high and low data rate applications. Here, we present an algorithm that can utilize the available channels in UWB systems. The algorithm is known as dynamic channel scheduling algorithm (DCSA). The proposed algorithm is based on a distributed dynamic channel allocation technique to distribute the channels among neighboring piconets. The purpose of the algorithm is to increase the spectral efficiency (SE) and the quality of service (QoS) of the system. We also present the algorithm in details and a numerical example to describe the algorithm is given

articleTitle: A Secure Admission Control Scheme for P2P Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper first points out that Kim et al's schemes will suffer from the Sybil attack and conspiracy attack, and then proposes a secure admission control scheme for P2P networks. The new scheme proposed not only can withstands Sybil attack and conspiracy attack, but also possesses all properties of Kim et al's schemes

articleTitle: PRATM - Derived PRASAN Error Concealment Model for Efficient Transmission of MPEG Video Streams Over ATM Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Efficient recovery of video sequences from compressed video, transmitted over data networks is one of the biggest challenges to researchers in the field. This paper addresses this problem in context of asynchronous transfer mode networks (ATM) and proposes a model for error free recovery of damaged/lost data. In ATM networks channel errors or congestion cause data to be dropped, which results in the loss of entire macro blocks of MPEG video being transmitted. The proposed model PRATM employs the bit mapping procedure defined in PRASAN error concealment model and applies the mapping algorithm to the intra frames of GOPs for providing enhanced compression by generating correlation polynomials. The major contribution of this paper is the inclusion of additional header block, containing the correlation information derived from the principle of bit level mapping for the payload data of high priority ATM packets carrying the video information. The high priority data, taken two (termed inverse pair) at a time are subjected to bit level mapping and the obtained correlation polynomial information is provided as the header in both the considered data. This is a measure taken to cope with extreme congestion condition when even a high priority packet could be lost in the channel

articleTitle: Wideband Stacked Double Disc-Ring Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A wideband dielectric resonator antenna is proposed in this paper. To enhance the bandwidth, two stacked resonators with different dielectric constants and sizes are used, and a coaxial probe is placed off the antenna axis to excite the HEM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11delta</sub> mode in the DRA. The effects of antenna parameters such as dielectric constant, probe length and excitation position as well as air-gaps are investigated. The analysis is performed numerically, using commercial software high frequency structure simulator. An impedance bandwidth as wide as 63% (from 6.9 GHz to 13.2 GHz, VSWR les2) is achieved with the proposed antenna

articleTitle: A Threshold Optimizing Method Based on Markov in AMC Combined with HARQ
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A Markov based method for modulation and coding scheme (MCS) selection is proposed for pilot assistant adaptive modulation and coding scheme (AMC) with hybrid ARQ (HARQ) retransmissions. A first-order finite-state Markov model (FSMM) is introduced to represent the time correlation character of channel fading during (channel quality indicator) CQI feedback and HARQ retransmissions. According to different QoS target, such as maximize the air interface throughput or maintains a target frame error rate (FER) for each user. The Markov based method can deduce different reference pilot thresholds for each MCS. Theoretical analysis and link level simulation results both show the efficiency of the Markov based method for pilot threshold calculation according to different QoS target and different HARQ retransmission times

articleTitle: On the Performance of MIMO-OFDM Beamforming Systems with Feedback Delay
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Transmit beamforming and receive combining in multiple input and multiple output orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) systems are an efficient way to combat fading in frequency-selective channel. In the absence of channel state information (CSI) at the transmitter, the receiver computes the optimal beamforming vectors for all subcarriers according to the known CSI and sends their information back to the transmitter through a feedback channel. However, in practical situation, the transmitter may acquire outdated information about the beamforming vectors when there is a delay in the feedback channel. In this contribution, we use the predicted channel to calculate the optimal beamforming vector at the receiver and send it in advance. In this way, the impact of feedback delay to the system can be cancelled out. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme with the feedback delay performs a little degradation than with the perfect feedback

articleTitle: Channel Estimation Based on Extended Kalman Filtering for MIMO-OFDM Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: MIMO-OFDM systems are considered as the solution scheme for future wideband wireless communication systems. And channel state information play a crucial role in data detection module. But Kalman filtering (KF) is a linear processing method which is not fit for processing nonlinear problem. While wireless channels have some nonlinear characteristics. Owing to the above reasons, this paper describes a channel estimation method based on extend Kalman filtering (EKF) for MIMO-OFDM systems. The proposed method based on EKF can exploit pilot symbols and an extended Kalman filter to implement channel estimation without the aid of any prior knowledge of channel statistics. In comparison with the channel estimation methods based on the least square (LS) and the least mean square (LMS) algorithms, the method base on EKF has better performances theoretically. Computer simulations also demonstrate the channel estimation method based on EKF outperforms the channel estimation methods based on LS and the LMS. Hence, the channel estimation method based on EKF can offer a dramatic system performance improvement at the cost of modest computational complexity

articleTitle: An Analysis of Multicast Support for Mobile Hosts Using Mobile IPv6
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Multicast can bring many attractive multimedia applications to network service and save the bandwidth. In the paper we address the issue of multicast support for mobile host using mobile IPv6 (MIPv6). MIPv6 offers two basic multicast methods for mobile host called bi-direction tunneling (BT) and remote subscription (RS), but each one has its complementary advantages and limitations. Firstly, the operations of BT and RS were analyzed in detail based on MIPv6. Then a multicast simulation model for mobile host was designed based on the mesh random network. Finally the cost performance and the delay characteristic of RS and BT were analyzed by using the random model. We also drew a conclusion that RS is more suitable for multicast than BT when the network resource optimization and the end-to-end delay were mainly considered for multicast communication

articleTitle: A Power-Consumption Analysis for 802.11DCF
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: To achieve the power-consumption performance of 802.11 DCF, it uses a box-ball model to resolve the packet collisions probability. In consideration of limited retransmissions for each packet, it approximates the state transform of active nodes as a finite-state one-dimension Markovian process. Following these models, the power-consumption performance of 802.11 DCF in a saturated WLAN environment is analyzed based on the concepts of virtual transmission period and average contention window. Results show that packet length and channel rate only has marginal effects on the power-consumption. When nodes are many, the power-consumption performance is mainly affected by the receive power of the node and has little relevance to the transmit power. Simulation results validate the analysis

articleTitle: Impact of Feedback Delay on System Performance with AMC/SR-ARQ over Rayleigh Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In cross-layered wireless networks, adaptive modulation and coding (AMC) and selective repeat-automatic repeat request (SR-ARQ) are employed to improve system performance generally. The article focuses on the impacts of feedback delay on such systems over Rayleigh fading channels. It is conducive to choosing more suitable modulation format in AMC by computing bit error rate (BER) based on the second-order statistics method when partitioning SNR levels. Accordingly, we provided N-success/N+1-failure throughput model for performance analysis in this paper. Then simulation results demonstrate that the system considering feedback delay not only does guarantee the average packet error rate (PER) constrains, but also improve system average spectral efficiency

articleTitle: A (t, n) Threshold Signature Scheme Against Conspiracy Attack
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A (t, n) threshold signature allows t or more members of the group cooperate to generate a signature on behalf of the group while providing the anonymity of the signers. Unfortunately, most of (t, n) threshold signature schemes proposed so far can not against the conspiracy attack, thus the group secret key can be revealed. The design of an efficient scheme is remained open. In this paper, we propose a new (t, n) threshold signature scheme. The feature of the proposed scheme is that part of members cannot conspire to get any system secret parameters, and cannot forge a valid signature. That is, it can against conspiracy attacks. The security of the proposed scheme is based on the difficulty of computing the discrete logarithm modulo for a composite number. The size of the group signature and the verification time of the group signature are equivalent to that of an individual signature

articleTitle: A Novel Channel Estimation Method for TD-SCDMA System
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The B. Steiner estimator used in the TD-SCDMA system assumes that the channel response during one timeslot is constant, which results in big errors under the fast varying channel condition compared with the real channel response. In order to solve this problem, a novel channel estimation method is proposed for the TD-SCDMA system. Every timeslot is separated into several segments, the multi-segment estimation and multi-slot LSM fit is used to improve the accuracy of channel estimation. By comparing this two methods and analyzing their effects to detection, especially for the joint detection (JD) algorithm of TD-SCDMA system, simulation results show that the novel channel estimation is more close to the real channel response, which can largely improve the system performance, especially for the fast varying channel environment

IEEE Keywords: Time division synchronous code division multiple access

articleTitle: A Linear Voltage Regulator for PLL in SOC Application
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In modern integrated circuit design, analog parts and digital parts are designed on a single chip. Many papers show that supply noises coupling from digital parts influence the performance of analog parts greatly. This paper presents a design to implement a linear voltage regulator with operational amplifiers for PLL in mixed signal integrated circuits, whose output voltage is proportional to bandgap reference. This circuit is designed in SMIC 0.18 mum CMOS process. The output voltage of the regulator can be stable when 1) power supply changes from 3.1 V to 3.5 V, and verse; 2) output current varies in the range from 15 mA to 300 muA. Its power supply noise rejection(PSNR) is less than -70 dB when frequency is below 1 KHz. The current consumption of this linear voltage regulator is about 1.7 mA

articleTitle: Congestion Aware Scheduling Algorithm for MANET
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In the mobile ad hoc networks (MANET), many characteristics, such as the multi-hop transmission of packets, high dynamic topology and the limited bandwidth, make the network performance very poor. Typically, packet schedulers in MANET give priority to routing packets over data packets and serve data packets in FIFO order. We find that the simple scheduling scheme performs poorly when the network is congested. This paper proposes a congestion aware scheduling algorithm (CARE) targeting to improve the performance of MANET. In the proposed scheduling scheme, a node takes into consideration the traffic load of its neighbors when deciding the passing flows' scheduling priority. All the incoming flows are first classified by the next hop address, then the scheduler sets their priority based on the rank of the neighbors' load. We study the performance of CARE through simulation experiments, and the results show that our scheduling scheme exhibits a significant performance improvement, compared to simple priority and drop-tail algorithm

articleTitle: Ordered Group Interference Cancellation for Quasi-Orthogonal Space Time Block Codes
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: We consider a multiple input and multiple output system with quasi-orthogonal space time block codes. Quasi-orthogonal space time block code (QOSTBC) is greatly used because it can achieve a good tradeoff between diversity and multiplexing. However, since the transmit code is not orthogonal, there exists interantenna interference at the receiver. By studying the post detection SNR of transmit symbols at each detection step of ordered interference cancellation (OSIC), we propose an ordered group interference cancellation (OGIC) at reduced complexity. Simulation results show that the proposed method can achieve near the performance of OSIC

articleTitle: An Efficient Preconditioner for RFICs Simulation Using Harmonic Balance Method
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: To overcome the limitation of Krylov subspace techniques using standard preconditioners in harmonic balance simulations of RFICs, a novel preconditioner, by virtue of a sparse-subsectional matrix, is introduced. This preconditioner, different from the ordinary block-diagonal matrix, not only gives a sufficient approximation to Jacobian matrix, but also exploits the characteristics of sparseness and subsectional condensation, which dramatically reduces memory usage and greatly improves factorization speed. Numeric experiments are included to demonstrate merits and efficiency of this new preconditioner

articleTitle: Energy-Efficient Scheduling of TCP Packet Transmission Over Satellite Channels
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In order to improve TCP performance over satellite network, optimization based data transmission should be designed to adapt the characteristic of satellite fading channel. This paper proposes an analytic model of TCP over satellite channel which associate TCP throughput with the significant parameters (transmission power, FEC, packet loss probability) under bandwidth constraints. Through the model a dynamic programming based approach is proposed and evaluated, which is able to maximize TCP throughput or fairness flexibly among base stations by solving a net utility function. A comprehensive simulation study using ns2 shows that the strategy achieves excellent goodput in the test scenarios and can provide fairness simultaneously through adjusting the algorithm parameter

articleTitle: Satellite Hyperspectral Imagery Compression Algorithm Based on Adaptive Band Regrouping
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Hyperspectral image from satellite is important for earth observation and military reconnaissance. However there exists big contradictory between the transmission capacity of satellite channel and large amount hyperspectral data. There are spatial and spectrum redundancy in hyperspectral image. As to exploit spectrum correlation sufficiently, it must be to pre-process hyperspectral image. In this paper, we propose a novel acceptable complexity lossy hyperspectral image compression scheme which combines the prediction based on adaptive band regrouping and JPEG2000-based coding algorithm. The regrouping includes band classification and reference frame selection. Our experiments show that the proposed approach has a good performance in quality and fidelity. It is effective and not complicated, which may be a good choice for hyperspectral compression in the embedded processor of satellite platform

articleTitle: Notice of Violation of IEEE Publication Principles: A MAC Aware Cross-Layer Routing Approach for Wireless Mesh Network
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract:

by Golnaz Karbaschi and Anne Fladenmuller,
in the Proceedings of the IEEE International Conference on Mobile Adhoc and Sensor Systems Conference (MASS), Nov. 2005
Wireless mesh networks (WMNs) are an emerging architecture based on multi-hop transmission. Improving the performance in face of unreliable wireless medium will support WMNs to be a very cost-effective solution for wireless ISPs. In this paper, we propose a new cross layer routing metric called expected transmission efficiency (ETE), which aims to find high throughput and low delay paths. ETE takes into account MAC-layer link quality as the number of packets retransmissions on wireless link and the contention level along the paths. The implementation of ETE metric in proactive routing protocol such as destination sequenced distance vector (DSDV) is also given. Simulation results show that our proposed cross layer routing metric achieves better performance in comparison to the traditional minimum hop metric

articleTitle: The Architecture of Planning and Deployment Platform for Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: With the actual applications of the wireless sensor networks growing, the challenges of the actual deployment get more and more. To improve deployment efficiency, reduce the deployment cost and evaluate the deployment risk, we propose the planning and deployment platform for wireless sensor networks. In this paper, we investigate the architecture of the planning and deployment platform for wireless sensor networks and its implementation framework. The architecture mainly contains four modules; network deployment, initialization, simulation and performance evaluation and optimization. This framework, which is based on J-Sim simulator, also provides the implementation details of these modules. In addition, an integrated workflow for the platform is illuminated to comprehend the architecture and framework clearly

articleTitle: Routing for Diverting Calls in ICAR System
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Integrated cellular and ad hoc relaying systems (ICAR) is a new wireless system architecture based on the combination of cellular and modern ad hoc relaying technologies. The ICAR system can balance loads of the system, increase the system's capacity cost effectively, reduce transmission power for mobile hosts and extend system coverage by using ad hoc relaying stations (ARS) to relay traffic from one cell cluster to another dynamically. Thus the ad hoc relaying stations are imported to accomplish diverting a call from a congested cell cluster (hot spot) to a noncongested one, a fast efficient relaying routing protocol which can factually reflect the cell's status is needed in ICAR networks. In this paper, a routing protocol designed based on DV (distance-vector) routing protocol is proposed for ICAR system. Then some simulation results are displayed to show the performance of the routing protocol. The results show that the protocol can provide a shortest path from a congested cell to a noncongested cell. The time delay of the call establishing is within a tolerable range that can basically meet the performance of ICAR system

articleTitle: A New Coding Scheme in SC-FDE
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate that SC-FDE has different error characteristic from OFDM.
