Accordingly, we point out that both comparisons of coded BER between OFDM with block interleaving and SC-FDE in the classical literatures are unfair. And then, we propose a new coding scheme, which could take the advantage of the constraint of the coded information bits, for SC-FDE. Convolutional codes with different coding rates (1/2,2/3,3/4) are employed in simulations. It will be demonstrated that this new coding technique is well suited to SC-FDE

articleTitle: An Extended DISCUS Scheme for Distributed Source Coding in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, the design and construction methods of the DISCUS (distributed source coding using syndromes) scheme in wireless sensor networks are analyzed. The encoder quantizes the continuous outputs of the source and calculates the syndromes of the source codewords. Only the syndromes are transmitted to the decoder. The decoder combines the received syndromes and the side information to reconstruct the original source information. Some modifications are adopted to refine the shortages of the original DISCUS scheme, called extended DISCUS (eDISCUS). Firstly, the decoding error on the most significant bit is corrected. Secondly, the simple mapping from decimal quantization levels to binary codebook is replaced by a Gray-like code. Thirdly, additional syndromes are transmitted to correctly decode all the single codeword error. Simulation results show that the modifications have better decoding error rate and distortion performances

articleTitle: A Novel Spatial Diversity Algorithms of Carrier Frequency Offset Synchronization for MIMO-OFDM Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: According to analyzing MIMO-OFDM systems signal model in the presence of carrier frequency offset, the spatial diversity algorithms of carrier frequency synchronization using one OFDM preamble sub-symbol correlation is proposed. This method is investigated into physical link implementation for carrier frequency synchronization with channel estimation for MIMO-OFDM systems. The simulation results are given in carrier frequency synchronization for MIMO-OFDM systems on wireless multipath mobile channel

articleTitle: Initialization Algorithm Based on SNIR Model for Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A newly deployed sensor network is unstructured and sensor nodes at the beginning are in the "blind" state, which have almost no knowledge about the topology of the network. The most urgent and important thing for deployment of sensor networks is to set up a coarse structure. In this paper, a practical algorithm to initialize the network and select cluster leader nodes is presented. The algorithm is analyzed on SNIR model, which addressed the specific characteristics in the deployment of wireless sensor network, such as nodes do not feature a reliable collision detection mechanism and may wake up asynchronously, and especially co-channel interference effect on transmission during initialization phase. A novel concept of interference-tolerant neighbor nodes is proposed to guarantee efficiency of the algorithm. The simulation result shows even in the restrict applicable model, clustering can be completed successfully

articleTitle: Boost the Performance of MBOK DS-UWB with Decision Feedback ISI Cancellation
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: M-ary bi-orthogonal keying direct sequence UWB (MBOK DS-UWB) systems have been considered a type of PHY suitable for future high-speed wireless personal area networks (WPANs). In multipath fading channels, high speed signals will suffer from serious intersymbol interference (ISI) and interpulse interference (IPI) phenomena which degrade the performance and cause "error floor". In this paper, we propose a decision feedback (DF) based scheme to achieve successive ISI cancellation (SIC). The proposed DF-SIC scheme can be used jointly with fractionally spaced (FS) Rake receivers. Performance is verified with simulations over the UWB single-user link with data rates of 110 Mbps and 220 Mbps. Numerical results show that the hybrid of DF-SIC and FS Rake can effectively boost the BER performance of MBOK DS-UWB in typical UWB channels

articleTitle: Time-Domain Investigating Path Loss Characteristics of UWB Signals in Indoor Line-of-Sight Environment
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Nowadays, the path loss characteristics of UWB signals is widely investigated in the world for providing the channel model to UWB system. In this study, the propagation rules for UWB signals in indoor line-of-sight (LOS) environment are proposed. The relationship between multipath overlapping and the path loss is analyzed mathematically in time-domain. A new 5 rays path loss calculation method, which is satisfactory accurate for indoor LOS environment, is developed based on time-domain theory. The simulation result shows that the path loss can be characterized as 3 zones with different path loss exponent as distance between transmitter and receiver (T-R) increasing, while the path loss exponent within the scope of 2 to 4

articleTitle: A Mobile IPv6 Firewall Traversal Scheme Integrating with AAA
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Recently, mobile IPv6 has been standardized to provide seamless roaming for mobile users in IPv6 network. However, current IP networks are predominantly based on IPv4 technology and most of the firewalls have been designed for these networks. These firewalls will interfere in the smooth operation of mobile IPv6 and can be a detriment to deployment. In this paper, we propose a mobile IPv6 firewall traversal scheme integrating with AAA protocol. By defining several diameter extension messages between the AAA server and firewall, the firewall policies can be adjusted dynamically to provide the mobile IPv6 entities with transparent communication. The solution requires neither any modification of mobile IPv6 protocol nor to add special network components. Furthermore, the scheme is based on hierarchical network model and taking AAA factors into consideration. Therefore, it suits the operation mode of many service providers as well

articleTitle: Analysis of DS-UWB with MMSE Equalization in Dispersive Channels
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, DS-UWB systems will be employed in dispersive channels. Due to the serious dispersive effect of multipath channels, DS-UWB systems with equalization are also considered. We propose an MMSE equalizer for solving the intersymbol interference (ISI), and this equalizer needs no statistical measurement. We also consider an equalizer of only essential partial taps to reduce the complexity of filter, and the simulation results show that the resulted performance is almost the same as the filter of all taps. The simulation of bit-error probability of DS-UWB systems in the dispersive channel verifies the analysis

articleTitle: A Novel Approach to Interference Mitigation with Coexisting Spectrum Users for UWB Pulse Radio
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, a novel approach to interference mitigation with coexisting spectrum users for UWB pulse radio is proposed. This new approach uses adaptive frequency spectrum estimator to give the estimating values of each coexisting spectrum users' center frequency and band. Based on these estimating values, the frequency band of UWB communication system can be adaptively divided into multibands. The center frequency and the pulse shape of each sub-bands are also determined adaptively. This method successfully solves the coexistence problem between UWB systems and the existing systems, especially for stochastic existing users, without the need of reducing UWB pulse power spectral density (PSD) over the whole UWB frequency band. Therefore, the application range of UWB systems can be enlarged by increasing the transmitted UWB pulse power

articleTitle: High Spectral Efficiency Transmission Scheme in Multiple Antenna CDMA Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: CDMA system combined with multiple antennas is very promising in the B3G and 4G wireless communication because its high spectral efficiency. Multiple antennas in CDMA system always perform on two sides: providing diversity gain or spatial multiplexing, which lead to the tradeoff between system BER performance and its capacity. In this paper, a new multiple antenna transmission scheme which not only provides better BER performance, but also higher capacity in CDMA system employing ZCZ (zero correlation zone) codes has been proposed. It fulfills the multiplexing by placing more than one symbol at each antenna each time and provides the diversity with each symbol on different transmitting antennas. With the character of ZCZ, the transmitting diversity can be assured. Analysis and simulation results show that, when there are two transmitting and receiving antennas, this scheme provides nearly two times the capacity comparing to MIMO-CDMA system, while system BER performance has also been improved

articleTitle: A Hybrid MQAM-LFSK OFDM Transceiver with Low PAPR
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: OFDM supports high data rate and generally requires no equalization at the receiver, making it simple and efficient. Besides its several benefits, it suffers from large peak-to-average-power ratio (PAPR) of the transmit signal, due to which its straightforward implementation becomes quite costly. There are several techniques to attack this problem. But, most of them are suited for specific applications or works with small number of subcarriers. Also, some need side information to be transmitted along with the signal to recover the signal properly. In this paper, a hybrid modulator is proposed that reduces PAPR while keeping the OFDM transceiver design simple, as it does not require any side information or a little side information to be sent and is efficient for arbitrary number of subcarriers. The results of the implementations are compared with conventional OFDM system as well as with other techniques like PTS

articleTitle: Blind Channel Equalization with Order Estimation Based on Evolutionary Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, a novel channel equalization algorithm based on evolutionary algorithm is proposed. By exploiting the excellent global optimization performance of the evolutionary algorithm, the order and impulse response of the equalizer are jointly evolved in different manners with the objective function of constant modulus algorithm (CMA) adopted as fitness function. The experimental results on simulated channel show that the proposed algorithm achieves satisfactory performance and robustness upon order information

articleTitle: A Hybrid Strategy of Location Database Clustering and Dynamic Hierarchical Caching in PCS Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The location database (LDB) organization has much impact on the performance of personal communication services (PCS) network. In order to optimize the LDB organization, users' moving and calling patterns should be considered together. In this paper, we propose a hybrid strategy of location database clustering and dynamic hierarchical caching for a hierarchical database structure in PCS network. The main goal of our strategy is to reduce the cost of location management and network signaling traffic of data access and communication. The strategy consists of two steps: (1) clustering location databases based on users' moving patterns in the system; (2) arranging the clusters and then caching the users' location information of the adjacent cluster at each cluster's representative node based on users' calling patterns. A threshold required for beneficial caching is used to determine whether to cache. Through experimental simulation, the comparison results demonstrate that our strategy can result in total cost reduction

articleTitle: Centroid Optimization Coverage and Polling the Sets of the "Coverage" Nodes: An Improved Coverage Scheme
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Wireless sensor networks have recently emerged as a premier research topic. Sensor networks also pose a number of new conceptual and optimization problems. Some, such as location, deployment, and tracking, are fundamental issues, in that many applications rely on them for needed information. One fundamental issue in sensor networks is the coverage problem, which reflects how well a sensor network is monitored or tracked by sensors. In this paper, we address one of the fundamental coverage schemes, namely centroid optimize coverage. It's an improved coverage scheme

articleTitle: A Multiple-Objective Fuzzy Decision Making Based Information-Aware Routing Protocol for Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: There can be multiple types of data in wireless sensor networks (WSNs) in order to probe the environment accurately, which are different in the energy, the delay and the bandwidth requirements and so on. This requires that routing protocols for WSNs be flexible in routing selection to meet the transmission requirements of the different data. This paper proposes a multiple-objective fuzzy decision making based information-aware routing protocol specifically for WSNs, MOFDMIA. In the protocol, sensor nodes are grouped into the clusters and each cluster has a gateway node. Multiple paths are generated between each node and the gateway node in a cluster, and sorted according to the different requirements of the data by multiple-objective fuzzy decision making (MOFDM). MOFDMIA then chooses the "best"path(s) to transmit the data with the different requirements. Simulation results have demonstrated the effectiveness of our approach for different types of data

articleTitle: Uncertain Data Management for Wireless Sensor Networks Using Rough Set Theory
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The wireless sensor networks (WSN) is a new emerging field with many sensor nodes deployed in a wide sphere to carry out a certain task. Considering the features of limited energy and densely deployed sensor nodes, the key challenge in wireless sensor networks is to reduce the power consumption and the high information redundancy. Furthermore, communication is widely viewed as the dominating power cost in many sensor networks applications, so it is obvious that it will save energy if data is aggregated before being sent to the sink node. As the illustrative examples are shown, rough set theory is a useful tool for local redundancy information de-correlation and can eliminate redundant transmission so as to provide a solution to uncertain data management for wireless sensor networks

articleTitle: A WPKI-Based Security Mechanism for IEEE 802.16e
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: IEEE 802.16e standard will enhance broadband wireless access solutions by taking advantage of the inherent mobility of wireless media. As the mobile services supported in the standard, new security problems may be coming and becoming a serious obstacle to develop the WMAN (wireless metropolitan access network). In this paper, security principles used in 802.16e is analyzed to find the vulnerabilities and threats to mobile WiMAX. A security mechanism against the threats is proposed based on WPKI (wireless public key infrastructure) technology to solve both security problems and the problems caused by the poor ability of the mobile terminal. By simulating the complete WPKI-based security process, the mechanism is proved to be competent for providing data privacy, integrity and non-repudiation protection between BS (base station) and MS (mobile station)

articleTitle: Multi-Path QoS Routing Protocol Under Three Different Path Selection Strategies in Wireless Ad-Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Compared to uni-path routing, multi-path routing can better utilize network bandwidth and balance network traffic. These features make it more suitable for mobile ad hoc networks with dynamic network topology and limited network bandwidth resource. In terms of QoS, providing multi-path routing in networks can better support QoS. In this paper, we propose a multi-path QoS routing protocol based on different path selection strategies for mobile ad hoc networks. According to different multi-path selection strategies, three sub-protocols have been designed. We evaluate the performance of the QoS routing protocol using extensive simulation

articleTitle: Characterization of Wireless Shallow-Water Communication Channel Based on Gaussian Beam Tracing
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Wireless acoustic signals propagation through the shallow water channels are strongly influenced by marine environmental factors. Understanding how the environment degrades different modulation schemes and to develop more robust schemes or select the appropriate scheme for the given conditions is very important. Based on the representative sound-speed profiles of the Taiwan Strait, this paper adopts Gaussian beam tracing model to compute a point source propagation eigenrays and obtain characteristics of underwater acoustic propagation loss for the flat and fluctuation of sea bottom under three differential sound-speed profiles conditions. Simulation results reveal the relationship between transmission loss and typical channel parameters, such as sound-speed gradient, sea bottom fluctuation, source depth and propagation distance, which provides a valuable guide for the practical design of underwater wireless communication systems

articleTitle: An Improved Long Transmission Protocol for VDL Mode 4
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: An improved long transmission protocol for very high frequency (VHF) digital link (VDL) mode 4 in aeronautical telecommunications network (ATN) is proposed, which includes a combined transmission scheme and a retransmission mechanism. In the combined transmission scheme, control messages can be piggybacked in conflict-free message transmission, and thus avoids the collision of RTS bursts and saves much more unused slots than original long transmission protocol. In the proposed retransmission mechanism, if destination station does not receive the DATA burst from the source station, it will send a CTS burst instead of a NACK burst in the slot initially reserved for ACK/NACK burst. Simulation results show that the improved long transmission protocol can greatly increase throughput and reduce average message delay

articleTitle: A Statistical Model for Indoor UWB LOS Channels
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: SV/IEEE 802.15.3a model has been the standard model for ultra-wide bandwidth (UWB) indoor non-line-of-sight (NLOS) wireless propagation, but for line-of-sight (LOS) case, it is not well defined. In this paper, a new statistical distribution model exclusive used for LOS environment is proposed based on investigation of the experimental data. By reducing the number of the visible random arriving clusters, the model itself and the parameters estimating of the corresponding model are simplified in comparison with SV/IEEE 802.15.3a model. The simulation result indicates that the proposed model is more accurate in modeling small-scale LOS environment than IEEE model when considering cumulative distribution functions (CDFs) for the three key channel impulse response (CIR) statistics

articleTitle: Blind Multiuser Detection for UWB Systems Based on Generalized Sidelobe Canceller
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper focuses on blind multiuser detection for ultra-wideband (UWB) systems over unknown multipath channels. Unlike conventional approaches, we propose a scheme based on generalized sidelobe canceller (GSC) due to its robustness and low complexity. In our work, a GSC array is employed to collect the multipath signals and suppress multiuser interference (MUI). Afterward, the unknown UWB multipath channel is estimated by eigenvalue decomposition (EVD), and a MMSE combiner is designed. Compared to other methods, the proposed approach can achieve satisfied performance with less computational cost, as simulations indicate

articleTitle: Implementation of Blind Equalization Algorithm for HF QAM Based on DSP
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, a modified CMA-DDLMS equalization algorithm based on the automatic switch according to SNR is proposed. This modified algorithm overcome the shortcoming of large residual error and preserves the fast convergence performance. The simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm on HF QAM signal The paper also gives the implementation procedure of the algorithm on TMS320C6711

articleTitle: Policy-Based Access Control Model for Mobile Agent System
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: As a new computing mode, the mobile agent technology attracts more and more attention of researchers. However, its complex and changeful computing environment brings forward a higher requirement for the flexibility and consistency of the system's security access control. To meet this requirement, this paper puts forward an access control model which can be applied in the mobile agent system (MAS). By making a description and conducting management of the policy which is independent of the access control enforcement mechanism, this model realizes access control mechanism with the policy as its core. Different from the existing access control models, through unified configuration over the access control policy, this model ensures the consistency of system security. Meanwhile, the model increases the flexibility of access control and realizes multi-policy supporting of security precaution

articleTitle: Improved Threshold Ring Signature for Ad-Hoc Group
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A number of peer to peer (P2P) systems as well as mobile ad-hoc networks (MANETs) fall into the category of ad hoc groups. Their needs for security have been widely recognized, so some signature schemes had been introduced for the ad hoc group. On the basis of analyzing those schemes, we propose a threshold ring signature from bilinear pairings for ad hoc groups. On the basis of analyzing the proposed scheme, we conclude that our scheme meets with the three requirements of threshold ring signature: correctness, anonymity and security against adaptively chosen message attacks in the random oracle model assuming the computational Diffie-Hellman problem (CDH problem) is hard to solve. Moreover, the small size on the signature, robustness, multi-signature and distributed computing characteristics of the proposed scheme, are useful for ad hoc notes to save communication overhead, memory size, computation, energy consumption and safety from widely known attacks

articleTitle: Kalman Filter Channel Estimation Based on Comb-Type Pilot in Time-Varying Channel
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In OFDM systems, time-varying channels destroy the orthogonality between sub-channels and cause interchannel interference (ICI). To compensate for this ICI, a Kalman filter based on comb-type pilot signal is proposed for channel estimation. The fast and frequency-selective fading channel is modeled as a one-order autoregressive (AR) process to reduce the complexity. Meanwhile, the result is refined using frequency-domain correlation and covariance matrix of estimation error in minimum mean-squared error sense. The simulation results show that this channel estimation method can achieve good performance

articleTitle: Full Diversity Concatenation Space-Time Coding Over Time-Selective Block Rayleigh Fading Channels via Duality
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A coding scheme for concatenation space-time codes to achieve the maximum diversity over the time-selective block Rayleigh fading channels via the time-frequency duality is proposed in this paper. Based on the basis expansion model (BEM) for the time-selective fading channels, we firstly inversely convert it into the corresponding virtual frequency-selective fading circulant matrix by pre- and post-multiplying IFFT and FFT matrix in the transmit and receive end respectively. And then with OFDM module, general space-time codes can be directly applied in it. Based on the pairwise error probability (PEP) analysis in case of rapid fading, we derive design and performance criteria for the concatenation space-time block coding. Extending the full diversity space-frequency coding approach proposed previously to our consideration, we construct the space-time-Doppler block codes from the general space-time codes through repetition, which achieve the maximum additional Doppler diversity besides space and time diversity. Simulation results demonstrate the excellent performance of the proposed technique

articleTitle: Blind Channel Estimation Based on Linear Precoding for OFDM Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Considering that channel estimation is crucial for coherent detection, a blind channel estimation method based on linear precoding for orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) systems is proposed in this paper. The proposed linear frequency-domain precoder is applied to each pair of blocks before they enter the OFDM system. Due to the introduced structure of precoder, the frequency-selective channel can be identified at the receiver based on cross-correlation operations, singular value decomposition (SVD) and resolving the scalar ambiguity. Because the linear frequency-domain precoder is creatively employed to channel estimation, the proposed blind method is computationally simple and requires no prior statistical information of channel or noise. And the proposed blind method has high spectral efficiency because it exploits no training sequence. Computer simulations have proved that this proposed blind method can identify the frequency-selective channels perfectly and have a good performance

articleTitle: Packet Scheduling for Multimedia Traffics in Downlink Multi-User OFDM Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, we propose and evaluate a new packet scheduling algorithm for multimedia traffics in multi-user OFDM wireless systems. Since there will be multiple quality of service (QoS) in the next generation mobile communications, especially at the downlink, how to schedule the resources to provide different QoS classes in an efficient and fair way is a crucial issue. This algorithm allocates the resources dynamically in both time and frequency domain based on the users' feedback channel information, fairness among users, packet urgency and loss rate of different QoS classes. It can satisfy multi-QoS requirements of both real-time and non-real-time traffics, keep fairness among users and maximize the system's throughput under the above conditions

Index Terms: Increase In The Number Of Users

articleTitle: A Novel Wideband MIMO Channel Model and the Wideband MIMO Software Defined Radio
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In the following, we present a novel wideband multiple-input, multiple-output (MIMO) channel model. The model is based on the eigenvalue decomposition (EVD) of the wideband channel correlation matrix. It does not assume the scatterers at the receiver fade independently of those at the transmitter. It also models correlation between delay bins in the power delay profile (PDP). With preliminary data gathered using the Wideband MIMO software defined radio (WMSDR) in fixed outdoor locations, we show good agreement between modeled and measured data

articleTitle: Cooperative Communication Using Distributed Differential Space-Time Codes
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, we propose a distributed differential en/decoding scheme for Alamouti's orthogonal space-time code using in a cooperative system. The relay terminal operates in the decode-and-forward (DF) mode. The proposed scheme does not require the knowledge of the channel state information (CSI) at either user or destination terminals

articleTitle: RDA: Reliable Data Aggregation Protocol for WSNs
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Data aggregation in wireless sensor networks is widely accepted as an essential paradigm for energy efficient routing but with low reliability under node and link failures. In this paper, we propose a protocol called RDA which associates packet's reliability in data transmission with the amount of information it contains and gives higher reliability to the packet which has more information by adjusting the degree of redundancy. Therefore, RDA can jointly optimize both information reliability and energy efficiency in sensor networks with data aggregation. Especially, RDA is not banded with special routing schemes; hence it can be used with any kinds of routing schemes supporting data aggregation in wireless sensor networks

articleTitle: The Research on Certainty-Based Secure Routing Protocol in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Secure routing protocol is one of research focuses in wireless sensor networks. The paper presents a secure routing protocol named CBSRP, which creates dynamic keys based on certainty. The protocol is implemented on MICAz suite. The performance of CBSRP is compared with those of other secure routing protocols through experiments finally

articleTitle: Improved Opportunistic Auto Rate Media Access Protocol for Multi-Rate Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Fairness of performance has been considered as a key object in multi-rate ad hoc networks. Some researchers proposed opportunistic auto rate (OAR) media access protocol, which is based on IEEE 802.11, to implement fair performance for each sender. However, OAR protocol still cannot avoid unfair performance in some topologies. In this paper, we improve OAR protocol in order to satisfy fair performance as far as possible. This modified OAR protocol is called improved opportunistic auto rate (IOAR) protocol. IOAR protocol consists of two interactive components: an equiprobable auto rate (EAR) protocol and a probabilistic mechanism. IOAR ensures equal bandwidth utilization rate, and each transmitter can share bandwidth according to its transmission rate. We perform a set of ns-2 simulations to study the efficiency of IOAR

articleTitle: An Ant Odor Analysis Approach to the Ant Colony Optimization Algorithm for Data-Aggregation in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper we present an ant odor analysis approach to the ant colony optimization (ACO) algorithm for data aggregation in wireless sensor networks. We provide a modification to the existing ACO data aggregation scheme by accounting for multiple sinks and sources in an energy-constrained wireless sensor network. By forming families of ants (FoA), an intrinsic way is provided to explore the search space for routing and for determining optimal data aggregation. An ant odor identification model (AOIM) serves to determine and increase the correlation between data at the various nodes by trying to include hitherto different data under the same family (FoA). Simulation results show that the energy-efficiency achieved is high with less associated costs even for a larger number of sources and sinks

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Data Acquisition Circuit Based on Nonperiodic Equivalent Sampling
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A new equivalent sampling circuit for nonperiodic UWB signal is presented in this paper. In order to sampling the UWB narrow pulse effectively, the sampling speed must be very high according to the Nyquist law, the equivalent sampling method is a valid solution in a simple way. However, the condition for the traditional equivalent sampling is that the signals to be measured are periodic or duplicate, so it's necessary to improve the equivalent sampling method to adapt to the nonperiodic UWB pulses train after PPM, which changed the intervals of pulses according to PN code. Experimental results of this implementing circuit are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method

articleTitle: Machinery Fault Diagnosis Using Improved LSSVM Method
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In fault diagnosis practice of recent years, the neural networks obtain many harvests, but it has a lot of questions in network structure selecting and network training. In the paper, the power spectrum of fault signals are decomposed by wavelet analysis, which predigests choosing method of fault eigenvectors, and a fault diagnosis model based on least squares support vector machine (LSSVM) is presented. Via structural risk minimization principle to enhance extensive ability, the model preferably solves many practical problems, such as small sample, non-linear, high dimension number and local minimum points. In the model, the non-sensitive loss function is replaced by quadratic loss function and the inequality constraints are replaced by equality constraints. The parameter of kernel function is chosen on dynamic to enhance the preciseness rate of diagnosis. The simulation results show the validity of the LSSVM model

articleTitle: Channel Estimation Error on Performance of Zero Force Beamforming Based Multiuser SDMA in Downlink
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In a MIMO OFDMA multiuser system, the multiuser diversity gain can be achieved both in spatial and frequency domain by joint spatial and frequency scheduling. Although the channel estimation error (CEE) may degrade such multiuser diversity gain, little work has been performed on it. In this paper, we investigate the effect of the CEE on MIMO OFDMA downlink based on multiuser zero force beamforming (ZFB). The effect of channel estimation error on the signal to noise ratio of the desired user is analyzed, and the system spectrum efficiency is evaluated for different CEE value. The simulation results show that ZFB is not sensitive to CEE when a reasonable CEE value is guaranteed in a cellular system. Compared to the multiuser diversity gain from joint spatial frequency scheduling, the performance degradation from CEE is acceptable

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Voice Over Wireless Networks Using NS-2 Simulation with an Integrated Error Model
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Wireless communication is the fastest growing field and with the emergence of IEEE 802.11 based devices, wireless access is becoming more popular. Many multimedia applications for IP networks have been developed and thus the demand for quality of service (QoS) has increased. In this paper our primary objective is to evaluate 802.11e EDCF framework for video, voice and background traffic all at the same time. Our assessment is based on an error model called E-model, MOS for VoIP and PSNR for video. We also studied the effects of random uniform error model on various types of traffic. As expected, wireless networks are more prone to errors than wired networks

articleTitle: Security Analysis and Improvement for Mesh Mode in IEEE802.16
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: IEEE 802.16 Standard as the advanced wireless air interface technology also faces the inherent security problem of wireless network, especially in its unclearly defined mesh network architecture. This article will focus on the mesh mode and continue the previous work (Fan Yang et al., 2005) to resolve the security problem. Through the analysis of the original scheme in mesh mode, an improved security scheme to resolve security problem in existed standard is proposed

articleTitle: A Study on the Security Features of the Parlay API Based Application Behavior
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: New security requirements arise with the opening of telecommunication networks via APIs. This paper presents the risk analysis of network security caused by Parlay API and proposes a Petri net based approach to analyze application behavior when interacting with Parlay API. With a time constraint predicate/transition Petri Net modeling, normal behavior and abnormal behavior are distinguished. A fuzzy set with membership function is defined to measure possible abnormality degree of application's behavior

articleTitle: Blind Channel Estimation for MIMO Uplink MC-CDMA Systems with Layered Space Frequency Equalisation
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, we investigate blind channel estimation for multiple input multiple output (MIMO) multi-carrier CDMA (MC-CDMA) systems in the uplink scenario. An autocorrelation contribution matrix (ACM) method is proposed in comparison with the subspace approach. Using only second order statistics, the ACM approach shows similar performance to that of subspace based approach. The added advantage is that it eliminates the need for rank estimation and noise power calculation as in subspace technique. In particular we incorporate blind channel estimation with layered space frequency equalisation (LSFE),which employs successive interference cancellation and therefore provides significant performance improvement over the conventional linear minimum mean square error (MMSE) based approach

articleTitle: Effects of Mobility on Mean Packet Delay Over Integrated Services Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Next generation cellular networks are based on packet switching and has QoS support based on architectures such as integrated services. To calculate the QoS parameters such as packet delay will be very important. In order reach to this goal, in this paper we propose a model for an integrated services wireless access router. Our model describes the user mobility effect on the mean packet delay over such routers under two different CAC schemes. Besides, we apply this model to evaluate the mobility effect over two QoS support approaches, the standard IntServ and a new proposal for QoS support based on integrated services named IntServ6

articleTitle: An Efficient Power Management Mechanism for WiFi-Based Handheld Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: We propose a system level dynamic power management scheme that considers interaction between CPU and WNIC, and types of workload to reduce energy consumption of handheld systems. The proposed scheme determines the clock speed (voltage) for the CPU and the power mode for WNIC according to the workload type. This mechanism works based on two observations: the consumed power of WNIC is reduced when the clock speed of CPU is increased, and the power modes of WNIC and the clock speed of CPU have different values based on the kind of workload. Experimental results show that on the average the proposed scheme reduces energy consumption by 8% for BE (best effort) workload, 3% for CBR (constant bit rate) workload, and 16% for interactive when compared to DVFS (dynamic voltage and frequency scaling) for CPU and DPM (dynamic power management) for WNIC

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Constellation Mapping and Channel Estimation in MB-OFDM UWB Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the influence of channel mismatch errors on the performance of multi-band OFDM (MB-OFDM) UWB systems according to different schemes of constellation mapping. The accuracy in the identification of time-invariant channel is limited either by errors in channel estimation or by noise. A model to analyze the effect of these factors is presented, from which the formula for bit error rate (BER) as a function of signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is derived. We also analyze the channel estimation based on block-type training sequence and comb-type pilots with linear interpolation, as shown by simulation that the comb-type estimator with appropriate pilot arrangement can achieve better performance than block-type estimator for the typical UWB indoor channel which exhibits low frequency selectivity relatively

articleTitle: Subband Based Adaptive Bit and Power Allocation for OFDM Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, by contrast with "subcarrier-to-subcarrier" allocation method, subband based bit and power allocation methods are discussed to decrease the computational complexity for OFDM systems. Hughes Hartogs algorithm (HHA) is modified for subband based allocation. Bit and power is adaptively allocated into subbands by two means: constant bit rate (CBR) adaptation and variable bit rate (VBR) adaptation. The simulations are carried out on a 1024-subcarrier OFDM platform and the results show that in the range of low average bit SNR (under 15 dB) over vehicular A channel the computational complexity overhead can be reduced by 80% or 90% at the cost of performance loss less than 1 dB or 3 dB respectively

articleTitle: Scalable Fair Random Early Detection
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper proposes the scalable fair random early detection (SFRED) to improve the fairness of RED. As a router generally sees packets from a fast flow more often than a slow flow, this suggests that the fairness of a RED router can be improved without per-flow information. In SFRED, fair bandwidth allocation is attained with a list that stores statistics of limited active flows. Based on this list, SFRED takes identifying and punishing the fast, unresponsive fast, and protecting slow flows into consideration. Simulations with simple IP networks demonstrate that the fairness of RED has been significantly improved with the implementation of SFRED. Different from the previous proposals the complexity of SFRED is proportional to the size of the list but not coupled with the queue buffer size or the number of active flows, so it is scalable and suitable for various routers

articleTitle: A Subspace Semi-Blind Adaptive Multiuser Detection Algorithm Based on Kalman Filter for MC-CDMA Uplink
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, a new subspace semi-blind adaptive multiuser detection based on a hybrid of Kalman filter and subspace estimation is proposed for MC-CDMA uplink. It is shown that the detector can be expressed as an anchored signal in the signal subspace and coefficients can be estimated by the Kalman filter. The spreading sequences of all known users are exploited to develop a new efficient semi-blind adaptive multiuser detection requiring fewer adaptive coefficients. To reduce the computational complexity, an improved projecting approximation subspace tracking with deflation (PASTd) algorithm is developed for adaptive signal subspace estimation. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed semi-blind multiuser detection offers substantial performance gains over the blind multiuser detection method in the MC-CDMA uplink environment

articleTitle: Energy Consumption Distribution-Aware Node Placement in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs)
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In some civilian applications of wireless sensor networks, the sensing nodes is so far away from the base station that relaying nodes must be employed to forward data. Some relaying nodes use up their power early because they have heavier traffic load, which affects the network lifetime. This paper proposes the two-phase placement strategy of relaying nodes, which implements an even energy consumption distribution among different nodes. Sensing nodes and relaying nodes consume the same power in every round of data transmission by adjusting location and data volume. Based on the strategy, this paper finds numerical relationship between the number of relaying nodes and network lifetime, offers a reference for the trade-off between increasing network lifetime and decreasing the number of relaying nodes

articleTitle: An Efficient Block-Matching Motion Estimation Algorithm for H.264 Video Coding Standard
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Block matching motion estimation (BMME) plays a very important role in video coding. The performance of BMME greatly affects the quality of the encoded bitstream. Full search (FS) is the optimal algorithm for BMME. But the tremendous computation payload of it is unaffordable for practical applications, especially for real-time applications. To overcome this problem, this paper presents an efficient motion estimation algorithm suitable for H.264/AVC encoding systems. The high computational demands of the H.264 video encoder are reduced by a deformable block matching algorithm using the node-based model. Experiments show that the efficient motion estimation algorithm presented can further reduce block matching distortion computations relative to conventional fast motion estimation algorithms with neglectable coding efficiency loss

articleTitle: A Novel Three-Stage Frequency Offset Estimator for OFDM
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A novel frequency offset estimate method is proposed for OFDM systems. In the proposed method, a special preamble composed of two training symbol blocks with several wide-sense identical parts is designed. To obtain a large estimate range together with a good estimation performance, a novel three-stage CFO estimate scheme based on the designed preamble is proposed. In this scheme, initial CFO estimates are first obtained over the two training symbol blocks by means of a novel two-stage estimate method. In the third stage, the two initial CFO estimates are jointly used to enlarge the CFO estimate range. Simulation results demonstrate that the novel three-stage frequency offset estimator has a satisfying estimate performance while achieving a large estimate range and maintaining a low computational complexity

articleTitle: Hierarchical Self-Healing Rings for Mobile Ethernet Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Beyond 3G system integrates various wireless accesses including 3G, 4G and wireless LANs and provides an all IP wireless solution for various Internet services. The ubiquitous and plug-and-play characteristics of Ethernet provide a unique opportunity to cover all access points of various radio systems. However, the mobile Ethernet still has the challenge of fault tolerance and survivability in migration to BSG systems. In this paper we propose a hierarchical self-healing ring (HSHR) architecture for mobile Ethernet networks. Based on the proposed heuristic algorithm called resilient cycle (R-cycle), fast automatic protection switching on the order of milliseconds, often in sub-50 ms, can be achieved in distributed resilience Ethernet rings. This paper also describes an implementation of R-cycle algorithm on our 10 Gbps network processor based multi-service Ethernet platform. It is shown that in the hierarchical self-healing ring (HSHR) architecture satisfactory performance and deterministic fast recovery can be guaranteed based on the proposed R-cycle algorithm

articleTitle: Position-Based Greedy Stateless Routing for Multihop WPANs Based on a Realistic OFDM UWB Physical Layer
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Almost all of the existing routing protocols are designed based on a simplistic and idealistic physical layer model, and with minimum hop count as the metric for route selection. Without modification, they cannot work well with a realistic physical layer. A position-based stateless routing protocol with greedy forwarding is proposed for multihop WPANs based on a realistic OFDM UWB physical layer. The transmission radius R is closely related to the link quality, and is defined by PER achievable. The optimum value of R is selected to be the distance to achieve a PER between 1% and 5% by trading off the throughput and PFR. The simulation results show that this position-based greedy routing scheme with carefully selected transmission radius R works well for multihop WPANs based on OFDM UWB physical layer. When on-demand routing protocols are considered, we believe that the link quality related metrics would work better than hop count metric

articleTitle: A Finite State Markov Chain-Based Umbrella Cell Channel Model for Fast Mobile Users
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper describes a new Markov propagation channel model for an umbrella cell environment for fast mobile users. The multistate model switches between propagation states representing open area, shadowing, and blockage. A linear combination of log-normal, Rayleigh, and Rice models is used to describe signal variations over an area with constant environment attributes while an M-state Markov chain is applied to represent environment parameter variations when the fast mobile moves from one microcell to another one in an umbrella cell. Channel parameters are evaluated for the experimental data and used in the simulation model. Results are presented in terms of signal waveform and bit-error-rate. The effect of DS-CDMA is also discussed. Simulation shows that our new channel model can be much more realistic than the classical models

articleTitle: Cluster Merging Algorithm with Link Optimization for Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Clustering sensor nodes is an effective approach for large-scale wireless sensor networks to enhance their performance. In this paper, we proposed CMA (cluster merging algorithm with link optimization), a new clustering algorithm for wireless sensor networks with low density and short communication range of sensor nodes. CMA is a multipoint initiated topology discovery algorithm, which merges small clusters to larger clusters with multi-hop intra-cluster communication by means of neighborhood discovery. During this course, it also optimizes wireless links in clusters to form a well distributed network topology. Residual energy is an important factor for regrouping clusters during network lifetime in order to balance the energy consumption of nodes. With the application of the algorithm, networks can form clustered topology fast and cluster heads can be well elected again after growing energy consumption. The simulation results show that CMA can shorten the topology establish time and reduce network overhead during the course

articleTitle: Effectiveness of the Limited Retransmission on the WLANs Using Error-Prone Channel
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: IEEE 802.11 based wireless local area networks (WLANs) is one of the most popular protocols for interconnecting portable communication devices. All the stations communicating over WLANs share a common wireless channel. Many conscious studies have been devoted to utilize this precious medium efficiently. However, most of these studies have been done either under assumption of idealistic channel condition or with unlimited retransmitting number. This paper is devoted to investigate influence of limited retransmissions and error level in the utilizing channel on the network throughput, probability of packet dropping and time to drop a packet. The results show that the networks using four-way handshaking mechanism has a good immunity against the error over the available range of retry limits, also the throughput is unchangeable with size of the network over the range of retransmission limits. On the other side, for the networks using basic access mechanism, the throughput is suppressed with increasing amount of errors in the transmitting channel over all the range of the retry limit as well as it is quite sensitive to the size of the network. However, the throughput does not change with retry limits when it exceeds the maximum number of the backoff stage in both DCF's mechanisms. In the both mechanisms the probability of dropping a packet is a decreasing function with number of retransmissions and the time to drop a packet in the queue of a station is a strong function to the number of retry limit, size of the network, the utilizing medium access mechanism and amount of errors in the channel

articleTitle: An Optimized Rate Control Algorithm for H.264 Under Low Delay Constraint
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: It is very critical to determine a suitable quantity parameter (QP) in the rate control of video compression. The first frame QP of a GOP (group of picture) affects subsequent frame QP of this GOP, therefore, it has an important impact on the compression video quality of entire video sequences. However, the existing rate control algorithms do not pay much attention to this issue. In this paper, the initial QP prediction (IQPP) algorithm that can predict the initial QP precisely is proposed based on statistics of encoded frames and frame complexity, and the remaining QP prediction (RQPP) algorithm adopts Lagrangian optimization techniques to choose the appropriate QP for I-frame of other GOPs. Our experimental results show the proposed algorithm greatly enhances the performance of rate control and rate-distortion optimization (RDO). Furthermore, the average peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) is improved and skipped frames are also reduced compared to traditional method under low delay constraint

articleTitle: Optimization of an AVS Audio Decoder on DSP
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The part III of Audio Video Standard of China (AVS) is the first Hi-Fi audio coding standard in China public domain. Through nonlinear quantization and context-dependent bitplane entropy coding (CBC), it offers distinct features of nonlinear quantization noise adaptation and high efficiency fine grain scalability (FGS), but also imposes great challenges on fixed-point implementation with high precision requirement and stringent computational resource restriction. This paper presents tuned optimization strategies for fixed-point arithmetic, buffer manipulation, entropy decoding, and CBC decoding loop reduction to address the challenges. The demonstration real-time implementation on fixed-point DSP TMS320C5509A shows that our design optimization cuts down computational complexity from over 200 MIPs to 60 MIPs while preserving over 15 effective bits precision for 16-bit PCM output

articleTitle: A Group Aware Topology Control Algorithm in Mobile Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In a mobile ad hoc network, the behavior of nodes is always characterized by group features, such as group mobility and communication in group. We propose a localized topology control algorithm, named group aware topology control (GATC), which takes the group features into consideration, and improves the connectivity of nodes in the same group. The structure derived from our algorithm, called GAG-f, is a connected power spanner, and its network capacity and intra-group connectivity can be adjusted through a parameter f. The simulation result also indicates that GATC could construct a topology to improve group connectivity according to the parameter f

articleTitle: Bandwidth-Guaranteed Multi-Path QoS Routing for Saving Energy in TDMA-Based Wireless Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: With the development of mobile ad hoc network (MANET), quality of service (QoS) provisioning and energy saving become more and more important. In the past, these two issues were treated separately. In this paper, we investigate a new way to combine the two together and present a novel on-demand bandwidth-guaranteed multipath QoS routing for saving energy (BMQRSE) in TDMA-based MANETs. The proposed scheme can provide QoS guarantee by reserving time slots and save energy by taking into account both the transmit power and the residual energy of the hosts along the multiple disjoint paths from a source to a destination. Simulation results show that BMQRSE has good network performance and balances the energy consumption of hosts

articleTitle: A Discrete-Time Queue with Discrete Autoregressive Process of Order 1 Fluid in High-Speed Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, we consider a discrete-time queue with discrete autoregressive process of order 1 (DAR(I)) fluid in high-speed networks. Close-form expressions for the probability generating function and mean queue length are derived. Finally, some numerical results are given and it is shown that the system performance is quite sensitive to the correlation of the arrival process

articleTitle: Construction of Large Girth (3,k) LDPC Codes Based on Cuboid
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The girth and minimum distance are two important factors of LDPC codes. In this paper we construct a type of LDPC codes with girth 8 based on cuboid. The codes are regular, whose column weight is 3. The minimum distance of the code with exact cuboid structure is only 8 and the distribution of code word weight is not optimal, so we proposed a scheme to improve the codes. The simulation results comparing the bit error rate (BER) performance over AWGN channels with randomly constructed LDPC codes shows that our codes are better than the randomly constructed ones

articleTitle: On the Tradeoff Between Robustness and Energy-Efficiency of the Routing Algorithm for Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In wireless sensor networks, the power-aware routing algorithm (PowerCost) can effectively reduce routing energy consumption and prolong the network lifetime, however, it can not tolerate localization errors. In contrast, the greedy routing algorithm is robust to localization errors but is not energy-efficient. In this paper, based on the analysis of the tradeoff between robustness and energy-efficiency, a robust power-aware routing algorithm, robust-powercost, is proposed, which combines the advantages of the previous routing algorithms. Extensive simulations are performed to confirm the efficacy of our algorithm and it is shown in the results that robust-powercost achieves near ideal performance for a wide range of system configurations

articleTitle: Adaptive Bandwidth Allocation for Multi-Media LEO Satellite Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Moving from single service systems to multiple services systems raises new challenges in multi-media LEO communication networks. Particularly, bandwidth allocation becomes more crucial for efficient use of wireless resources. In this paper, an adaptive bandwidth allocation method is presented. The approach is based on the fact that the bandwidth of a multimedia call is alterable in LEO systems and the bandwidth allocation problem is formulated as a constrained nonlinear optimization problem which aims at maximizing the satisfaction degree of the system. A genetic algorithm is developed to solve the optimization problem. Simulations have been outlined and the conformance to QoS parameters for the proposed approach has been verified

articleTitle: Scheduling for Wireless Networks Using Fuzzy Logic
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Scheduling for wireless networks is not as mature as for wired links networks. The main difference between wired links and wireless links is that wireless channel can exhibit high rate of link errors, resulting in unpredictable loss of link capacity. It makes scheduling more difficult in wireless links than in wired links. In this paper, we use fuzzy logic controller (FLC) to adjust link capacity allocated to each flow according to fluctuating channel state so as to maintain the fairness and not to waste the valuable resources

articleTitle: A High-Resolution Iterative DOA Algorithm for CDMA System
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, an iterative high-resolution DOA algorithm is presented for DOA estimation for CDMA systems. The algorithm iteratively removes detected signals from the received data and searches the residue spatial spectrum for further signals. It does not require any computationally expensive eigen decomposition or spatial smoothing in coherent multipath scenarios. Results are presented illustrating high-resolution at significantly lower SNR levels than those obtained by classical DOA algorithms such as MUSIC and MVM

articleTitle: A Simple Broadband Transition from Waveguide to Microstrip Line in X Band
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A simple broadband transition from waveguide to microstrip using the short transformer technique is proposed and investigated in this paper. A layer of dielectric substrate is employed as a matching structure between the waveguide and microstrip line structure, which is optimised using the direct search method. It is shown that the transition has an average return loss value of -19.2 dB throughout the X band (8-12 GHz) with the best return loss value of -64 dB

articleTitle: Research on Fast DCA Algorithms in TD-SCDMA Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Dynamic channel allocation is an important part of RRM (radio resource management) in TD-SCDMA systems. It consists of slow DCA and fast DCA. In this paper, the fast DCA in CAC procedure is studied, several algorithms are proposed. The performance of each algorithm is simulated; meanwhile, comparisons and analysis are given

IEEE Keywords: Time division synchronous code division multiple access

articleTitle: A New Intra Coding Method for Spatial Scalability in Scalable Video Coding
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In scalable video coding, spatial scalability is a layered video representation with several layers corresponding to different spatial resolutions for the same video sequence. Therefore, spatial correlation between successive two layers exists naturally, and should be further exploited. In this paper, a new scalable intra coding method for spatial scalability is proposed. It consists of two spatial layers: one base layer and one enhancement layer. The proposed intra coding method is fully compatible with H.264/AVC standard in base layer, while in enhancement layer the upsampled reconstructed base layer blocks are used for intra prediction under condition of that the adjacent prediction pixels are not available. The effectiveness of the new technique is demonstrated by experimental results. With almost no changes on both computation complexity and encoded bit-rate, the average increase of Y-PSNR is about 0.13 dB for sequence Football and 0.11 dB for Foreman

articleTitle: Analysis of IEEE 802.15.3 CAP Based on DC-OFDM-UWB
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, we present a way to estimate the performance of successful requests in contention access period (CAP) of IEEE 802.15.3 accounting for dual carrier-orthogonal frequency division multiplexing-ultra wide band (DC-OFDM-UWB). It is important for a piconet coordinator (PNC) to schedule traffic of a piconet and will determine the duration of contention free period (CFP). Simulation results show that the analysis accurately predicts the performance of CAP in UWB PHY. This research should provide helpful insight to the implementation of UWB-based IEEE 802.15.3 wireless networks

articleTitle: HOPA: A Near Optimization Algorithm for Pathfinding
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Based on the classic Dijkstra algorithm, this paper introduces the decision mechanism of AI into pathfinding, proposes a heuristic optimistic pathfinding algorithm, HOPA, puts forward the conditions of getting the optimum solution from this algorithm and further gives the proof. These two algorithms are tested contrastively, and the results show that the algorithm proposed in this paper may have a good prospect in some fields

articleTitle: Cycle Properties Analysis of Matrix-Filled LDPC Codes
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, we present the upper and lower bounds of the girth of MF-LDPC codes which are determined by the shift times of cyclic shift matrices by analysis the properties of cyclic shift matrices in cycle, we also propose a concrete conditional-filling construction, the simulations prove that sufficient utilization of the properties can reduce the amount of least cycle of the MF-matrix remarkably and improve the performance to a larger extent

articleTitle: BER Performance Analysis of RCPC Encoded MIMO-OFDM in Nakagami-m Channels
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In order to improve the bit error rate (BER) of multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency diversity multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) system in Nakagami-m channels, the model used rate-compatible punctured convolution (RCPC) and space-time block code (STBC) at the transmitter, maximum ratio combining (MRC) at the receiver was put forward. The signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the MIMO-OFDM system in Nakagami-m channels was studied, the expression of BER was given and the average BER upper limit after RCPC encode was further presented. Simulation result shows that the BER performance and the diversity gain of MIMO-OFDM with RCPC encoding achieve much improvement than the system with no RCPC. Owing to the free distance becomes shorter with the increase of code rate, the BER performance and the diversity gain of RCPC encoded MIMO-OFDM decreases a little

articleTitle: A Pilot Aided Multi-Cell Interference Cancellation with LMS Channel Estimation for STC OFDM Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper proposed a new LMS based adaptive CCI cancellation algorithm for space-time block coded orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (STC OFDM) systems. We apply LMS based adaptive channel estimation by orthogonal pilot patterns to identify channel information of interference cells. And by the identical channel information of different cells, we can easily reconstruct the signal of received signal, and then subtract co-channel interference cancellation (CCI) signal from the received signal. Simulation result shows that the proposed approach can achieve enhancement of system performance

articleTitle: Voronoi Tessellation Based Haar Wavelet Data Compression for Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: We propose a distributed wavelet-based algorithm which can transform irregularly sample data using Haar wavelet-based compression solutions in this paper. We consider the characteristics and location information of nodes in sensor networks, a new distributed data aggregation mode based on "area" is used firstly. On the basis of these new models, a novel wavelet-based irregularly sample data compression and data transform model DDCM is proposed for sensor networks. Theoretical analyses and simulation results show that, the above new methods have the good ability of approximation, and can compress the data efficiently and can reduce the amount of data greatly. So, it can prolong the lifetime of the whole network to a greater degree

articleTitle: DSP Implementation Aspects of an OFDM Based Wireless MAN Modem
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: For future broadband telecommunication systems and networks based on OFDM technology, efficient implementation of an OFDM modems is a major requirement. In this paper, we are going to present some fundamental aspects of implementation of an OFDM based wireless MAN modem on TI digital signal processors (DSP) C6000 family. To this purpose, we model a typical MMDS system based on IEEE802.16a standard, and simulate it in TI code composer studiotrade (CCS) environment with C programming language and compare the floating and fixed point implementation aspects of the system. This is useful and enhances rapid prototyping of a DSP based wireless MAN modems. The wireless MAN system will be demonstrated a high speed wireless communication system. One basic component of common OFDM systems is the computation of the DFT and IDFT which was our main focus in this paper via considering some efficient FFT algorithms like the Radix-2 and the Radix-4. In the next part, we compare various methods of implementing of a simple channel estimation and equalization for compensation of the signal affected by frequency selective fading channel model which were employed in our simulation

articleTitle: A Reliable Localization Method in WSNs
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: It is necessary to secure the localization in adversarial settings. This paper aims to developing a localization method which can withstand common attacks, such as eavesdropping or tempering localization information, through its own mechanism

articleTitle: A Cross-Layer Design for Broadcast Algorithm in MANETs
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In mobile ad hoc networks, due to the dynamic nature of ad hoc networks, many unicast and multicast protocols depend on broadcasting mechanism to finish control and route establishment functionality. A straightforward broadcasting, however, will be very inefficient and costly and easily result to the broadcast storm problem. In this paper, we propose the JDCT-C algorithm. It is a distributed algorithm and adopts cross-layer design. According to the receiving signal strength from the physical layer and neighboring nodes information from the network layer, it decides whether a node can retransmit the message or not without needing any global information and control messages and dynamically adapts the backoff defer in the MAC layer. The simulation experiments have demonstrated the efficiency of the proposed broadcast algorithm meanwhile the broadcast storm problem is significantly alleviated

articleTitle: The Block Coding Used in OFDM System to Reduce the PAPR
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper first introduces some efficient technologies to reduce the peak-to-average power ratio in OFDM system, and then gives the basic concepts of block code, which could reduce the PAP ratio by mapping the maximal peak power codes to average power codes. The paper gives the block chart of the system and the simulated result of the block codes

articleTitle: Generalized Affine Spectral Correlation Analysis with Application to Multifractal Signal Processing
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new set of tools for spectral correlation analysis: the generalized affine spectral correlation analysis. Based on the affine Wigner distributions of J. and P. Bertrand and the pseudo affine Wigner distribution of Paulo Goncalves, generalized spectral correlation analysis was proposed. To formalize their place within the echelon of the affine class of time-scale distributions (TSD's), we introduce and study an alternative set of spectral correlation generators and kernel for this class. With application to the multifractal signal processing, it's proved that the generalized affine spectral correlation analysis is a useful tool for signal processing

articleTitle: Joint Design for LDPC Coded OFDM with Transmit Adaptive Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A novel design is proposed for the OFDM system using structured LDPC codes with the transmit adaptive antennas (TxAA), which can achieve improved performance by adaptively using the feedback subcarrier frequency information at the transmit side. With the aid of the closed multiple antenna technique, much gain can be achieved in the coded OFDM system. Furthermore, irregular LDPC codes have the advantage of unequal error protection (UEP) for coded bits with different degree distributions. Thus mapping the coded bits with high degrees to the subcarriers with weak subchannel attenuation is proposed to fully utilize the feedback information not only in the design of the closed-loop OFDM transmission but also in the combination design of the coding scheme and OFDM modulation. The proposed scheme is proven to be effective by simulation results in the frequency selective channel scenario
